chapters.title: Chapter 1 · The Genealogy and Birth of Jesus
chapters.intro: The chapter opens with a family line: from Abraham, the ancestor of the Jews, through King David, generation by generation down to Joseph, in three groups of fourteen. Then it tells how Jesus was born: Mary was betrothed to Joseph and was found to be pregnant before they lived together; Joseph meant to end the betrothal quietly, but an angel told him in a dream that the child was from the Holy Spirit and was to be named Jesus.

verses.en: The book of the genealogy of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham.
Abraham fathered Isaac, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers,
and Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar, and Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Aram,

cmp.note: 古代的家谱通常只写父亲。这份家谱却在耶稣的母亲以外提到四个女人：他玛、喇合、路得和「乌利亚的妻子」（第 3、5、6 节），她们的故事都在旧约里。
cmp.en: Ancient genealogies normally name only fathers. This one mentions four women besides the mother of Jesus: Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and "the wife of Uriah" (verses 3, 5 and 6), whose stories are all told in the Old Testament.

verses.en: and Aram fathered Amminadab, and Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon,
and Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab, and Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse,
and Jesse fathered David the king. And David fathered Solomon by the wife of Uriah,

cmp.note: 字面是「从那属于乌利亚的女人」，没有写她的名字。旧约《撒母耳记下》11–12 章说她叫拔示巴，原是大卫手下将领乌利亚的妻子。
cmp.en: Literally "by her who was Uriah’s"; her name is not given. 2 Samuel 11–12 calls her Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, one of David’s officers.

verses.en: and Solomon fathered Rehoboam, and Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph,

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里写的是 Asaph，第 10 节写的是 Amōs；多数抄本分别是 Asa、Amōn，和旧约里这两位王的名字（亚撒、亚们）一致，和合本跟的是后一种。白话照和合本的人名写，英文照底本的拼法。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads Asaph here and Amos in verse 10; most manuscripts read Asa and Amon, the names these two kings have in the Old Testament, and the Union Version follows those with 亚撒 (Yàsā) and 亚们 (Yàmén). The Chinese keeps the Union Version’s names; the English keeps the edition’s spelling.

verses.en: and Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, and Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah,
and Uzziah fathered Jotham, and Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah,
and Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, and Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah,
and Josiah fathered Jechoniah and his brothers, at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
And after the deportation to Babylon, Jechoniah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel,
and Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, and Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor,
and Azor fathered Zadok, and Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud,
and Eliud fathered Eleazar, and Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob,
and Jacob fathered Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.

cmp.note: 前面一路都是「某人生某人」，到这里句式变了：没有说「约瑟生耶稣」，而说耶稣是「从马利亚生的」。原因在下面第 18–25 节交代。
cmp.en: Up to here the pattern has been "A fathered B." Here it changes: the text does not say "Joseph fathered Jesus" but that Jesus "was born of Mary." Verses 18–25 explain why.

verses.en: So all the generations from Abraham to David are fourteen generations, and from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to the Christ fourteen generations.
Now the birth of Jesus Christ was in this way. When his mother Mary had been betrothed to Joseph, before they came together she was found to be with child from the Holy Spirit.
And Joseph her husband, being righteous and not wanting to expose her to disgrace, resolved to dismiss her quietly.

But as he was considering these things, look, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, “Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for what is conceived in her is from the Holy Spirit;
and she will bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins.”

cmp.note: 「耶稣」这个名字来自希伯来话，意思是「上主拯救」，所以天使接着说「因为他要把自己的百姓……救出来」。这层意思在希腊文、中文、英文里都看不出来。
cmp.en: The name Jesus comes from Hebrew and means "the Lord saves," which is why the angel goes on, "for he will save his people." The link cannot be seen in the Greek, the Chinese or the English.

verses.en: Now all this took place so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
“Look, the virgin will be with child and will bear a son, and they will call his name Emmanuel,” which is translated, “God with us.”

cmp.note: 这句话引自旧约《以赛亚书》7:14。希腊文 parthenos 是「童女」；希伯来原文那个词的意思是「年轻女子」。这里引的是当时通行的旧约希腊文译本。
cmp.en: The words are quoted from Isaiah 7:14. Greek parthenos means "virgin"; the word in the Hebrew original means "young woman." The quotation follows the Greek translation of the Old Testament that was in common use at the time.

verses.en: And Joseph, having risen from sleep, did as the angel of the Lord commanded him and took his wife,
and he did not know her until she had borne a son; and he called his name Jesus.

cmp.note: 字面是「没有认识她」，是从希伯来话来的委婉说法，指夫妻同房。英文照字面写，白话直接写「同房」。
cmp.en: Literally "did not know her," a euphemism carried over from Hebrew for sexual relations. The English keeps it; the Chinese says it outright with 同房 (tóngfáng, "share a bed").

chapters.title: Chapter 2 · The Magi; the Flight to Egypt
chapters.intro: Jesus is born in Bethlehem. Magi from the east follow a star, looking for the child “born king of the Jews”; King Herod is alarmed and tries to use them to find the child. The magi pay the child homage and go home another way. Warned in a dream, Joseph flees to Egypt with the child and his mother, and Herod kills the boys of Bethlehem. After Herod dies they return and settle in Nazareth.

verses.en: Now when Jesus was born in Bethlehem of Judea in the days of Herod the king, look, magi from the east arrived in Jerusalem,

cmp.note: 原文 magoi 指东方（波斯、巴比伦一带）懂星象、会解梦的学者，和合本译「博士」。经文没有说他们有几个人，也没有说他们是王；「三位」是后来的传说。
cmp.en: Greek magoi were learned men of the East (Persia, Babylonia) skilled in the stars and in dreams; the Union Version calls them 博士 (bóshì, "scholars"). The text does not say how many there were or that they were kings; "three" is a later tradition.

verses.en: saying, “Where is he who has been born king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to pay him homage.”

cmp.note: 这几个字可以读成「在东方」（和合本、白话、英文都这样译），也可以读成「在它升起的时候」。
cmp.en: The phrase can be read "in the east" (as both Chinese versions and the English take it) or "at its rising."

verses.en: And when King Herod heard it, he was troubled, and all Jerusalem with him;
and gathering all the chief priests and scribes of the people, he inquired of them where the Christ was to be born.
And they said to him, “In Bethlehem of Judea, for so it is written through the prophet:
‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means least among the rulers of Judah; for from you will come a ruler who will shepherd my people Israel.’”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《弥迦书》5:2，最后一句并用了《撒母耳记下》5:2 的话。伯利恒是大卫王的家乡。
cmp.en: Quoted from Micah 5:2, with the last clause drawing on 2 Samuel 5:2. Bethlehem was the home town of King David.

verses.en: Then Herod, secretly calling the magi, learned from them exactly the time when the star appeared,
and sending them to Bethlehem he said, “Go and search carefully for the child; and when you have found him, report to me, so that I too may come and pay him homage.”
And having heard the king, they went on their way; and look, the star that they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the child was.
And seeing the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
And coming into the house they saw the child with Mary his mother, and falling down they paid him homage; and opening their treasures they offered him gifts, gold and frankincense and myrrh.
And being warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they went back to their own country by another way.

Now when they had gone, look, an angel of the Lord appears to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and flee to Egypt, and stay there until I tell you; for Herod is about to search for the child, to destroy him.”
And he rose and took the child and his mother by night and departed for Egypt,
and was there until the death of Herod, so that what was spoken by the Lord through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, “Out of Egypt I called my son.”

cmp.w: Ex Aigyptou ekalesa ton huion mou
cmp.note: 引自旧约《何西阿书》11:1。那里的「我的儿子」原是指以色列民族：上帝把他们从埃及领出来。
cmp.en: Quoted from Hosea 11:1, where "my son" originally means the people of Israel, whom God brought out of Egypt.

verses.en: Then Herod, seeing that he had been tricked by the magi, was greatly enraged, and he sent and killed all the boys in Bethlehem and in all its region who were two years old and under, according to the time that he had learned exactly from the magi.
Then was fulfilled what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying,
“A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning, Rachel weeping for her children; and she would not be comforted, because they are no more.”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《耶利米书》31:15。拉结是以色列人的一位女祖先，拉玛是伯利恒北边的一个地方；那里原是说她为被掳走的子孙哭。
cmp.en: Quoted from Jeremiah 31:15. Rachel was one of the mothers of the people of Israel, and Ramah is a place north of Bethlehem; in Jeremiah she weeps for her descendants carried off into exile.

verses.en: Now when Herod had died, look, an angel of the Lord appears in a dream to Joseph in Egypt,
saying, “Rise, take the child and his mother, and go into the land of Israel, for those who were seeking the child’s life have died.”
And he rose and took the child and his mother and came into the land of Israel.
But hearing that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there; and being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the region of Galilee,
and he came and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophets might be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”

cmp.note: 旧约里找不到一字不差的这句话，经文也只说「先知们」，没有指明是哪一位；它指的是哪一处，历来说法不一。
cmp.en: No sentence in the Old Testament matches this word for word, and the text says only "the prophets" without naming one; which passage is meant has long been debated.

chapters.title: Chapter 3 · John the Baptist; Jesus Is Baptized
chapters.intro: John the Baptist proclaims in the wilderness of Judea that the kingdom of the heavens is near and people must repent; crowds come to be baptized by him in the Jordan. He rebukes the Pharisees and Sadducees who come, and says that one stronger than he is on the way. Jesus arrives from Galilee to be baptized; John at first tries to stop him. As Jesus comes up from the water the heavens open and a voice says, “This is my beloved Son.”

verses.en: Now in those days John the Baptist appears, proclaiming in the wilderness of Judea
and saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near.”

cmp.note: 字面是「诸天的国」。这卷书多半用这个说法，意思和别的福音书里的「上帝的国」一样；当时的犹太人常用「天」来代称上帝。和合本、白话写「天国」，英文照字面。
cmp.en: Literally "the kingdom of the heavens." This Gospel mostly uses this phrase where the others say "the kingdom of God"; Jews of the time often said "heaven" in place of "God." Both Chinese versions write 天国 (tiānguó, "heaven’s kingdom"); the English keeps the wording.

verses.en: For this is he who was spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, saying, “A voice of one calling out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.’”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《以赛亚书》40:3。
cmp.en: Quoted from Isaiah 40:3.

verses.en: Now John himself had his clothing of camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist, and his food was locusts and wild honey.
Then Jerusalem and all Judea and all the region around the Jordan were going out to him,
and they were being baptized by him in the Jordan River, confessing their sins.
But seeing many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming to his baptism, he said to them, “Offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Bear fruit, then, worthy of repentance,
and do not presume to say to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father,’ for I say to you that God is able from these stones to raise up children for Abraham.
Already the axe is laid at the root of the trees; every tree, then, that does not bear good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but he who comes after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not fit to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”
Then Jesus arrives from Galilee at the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
But John tried to prevent him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and do you come to me?”
But Jesus answered and said to him, “Let it be so now, for thus it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he lets him.
And when Jesus was baptized, immediately he went up from the water; and look, the heavens were opened, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove, coming upon him;
and look, a voice from the heavens, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”

cmp.note: 《马可福音》1:11 里这句话是对耶稣说的（「你是我亲爱的儿子」），这里是对在场的人说的（「这是我亲爱的儿子」）。
cmp.en: In Mark 1:11 the voice speaks to Jesus ("You are my beloved Son"); here it speaks about him to those present ("This is my beloved Son").

chapters.title: Chapter 4 · The Testing; Jesus Begins in Galilee
chapters.intro: The Spirit leads Jesus into the wilderness, where he fasts forty days; the devil tests him three times, and three times he answers with words of scripture. After John is arrested he returns to Galilee, settles in Capernaum by the lake, and begins to proclaim that the kingdom of the heavens is near. He calls four fishermen to follow him and goes through all Galilee teaching and healing, and crowds from many regions follow him.

verses.en: Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit, to be tested by the devil.
And having fasted forty days and forty nights, afterward he was hungry.
And the tempter came and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell these stones to become loaves of bread.”
But he answered and said, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that comes out through the mouth of God.’”

cmp.note: 耶稣三次回答引的都是旧约《申命记》（8:3、6:16、6:13），那几章讲的是以色列人在旷野里四十年受考验。魔鬼在第 6 节引的是《诗篇》91:11–12。
cmp.en: All three of Jesus’s answers quote Deuteronomy (8:3; 6:16; 6:13), chapters about Israel’s forty years of testing in the wilderness. In verse 6 the devil quotes Psalm 91:11–12.

verses.en: Then the devil takes him into the holy city and set him on the pinnacle of the temple,

and says to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down; for it is written, ‘He will command his angels concerning you, and on their hands they will bear you up, so that you will not strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus said to him, “Again it is written, ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Again the devil takes him to a very high mountain and shows him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory,
and he said to him, “All these I will give you, if you fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus says to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him only shall you serve.’”
Then the devil leaves him, and look, angels came and were attending him.
Now when he heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew into Galilee.

cmp.note: 原文是「被交出去」，没有说交给谁；和合本直接写成「下了监」。这个动词后面还要用在耶稣自己身上。
cmp.en: The Greek is "was handed over," without saying to whom; the Union Version writes 下了监 (xià le jiān, "was put in prison"). The same verb is later used of Jesus himself.

verses.en: And leaving Nazareth he came and settled in Capernaum by the sea, in the territories of Zebulun and Naphtali,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
“Land of Zebulun and land of Naphtali, the way of the sea, beyond the Jordan, Galilee of the nations,

cmp.note: 第 15–16 节引自旧约《以赛亚书》9:1–2。加利利一带犹太人和外族人混居，所以叫「外族人的加利利」。
cmp.en: Verses 15–16 are quoted from Isaiah 9:1–2. Jews and non-Jews lived side by side in Galilee, hence "Galilee of the nations."

verses.en: the people sitting in darkness saw a great light, and for those sitting in the region and shadow of death, light has risen for them.”
From then Jesus began to proclaim and to say, “Repent, for the kingdom of the heavens has come near.”
And walking by the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon who is called Peter and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
And he says to them, “Come after me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
And immediately they left the nets and followed him.
And going on from there he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets; and he called them.
And immediately they left the boat and their father and followed him.
And he went about in all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness among the people.

And the report about him went out into all Syria; and they brought to him all who were sick, afflicted with various diseases and pains, those possessed by demons and epileptics and paralytics, and he healed them.
And large crowds followed him from Galilee and the Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea and from beyond the Jordan.

chapters.title: Chapter 5 · The Sermon on the Mount (1): The Blessed; the Law Fulfilled
chapters.intro: Jesus goes up the mountain, sits down and begins to teach his disciples; the speech runs to the end of chapter 7. He first names nine kinds of people who are “blessed,” and calls the disciples salt and light. He then says he has come not to abolish the Law but to fulfill it, and in six sets of “You have heard … but I say to you” he speaks of murder, adultery, divorce, oaths, retaliation and love of enemies. From verse 3 on, Jesus is the only speaker.

verses.en: Now seeing the crowds, he went up on the mountain; and when he had sat down, his disciples came to him,
and opening his mouth he was teaching them, saying,
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.

cmp.note: 字面是「在灵里贫穷的人」，和合本译「虚心的人」。原文的「贫穷」是指一无所有、要靠人周济的那种穷。
cmp.en: Literally "the poor in spirit"; the Union Version has 虚心的人 (xūxīn de rén, "the humble-minded"). The Greek word for "poor" means destitute, dependent on others for support.

verses.en: Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be filled.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called sons of God.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted for the sake of righteousness, for theirs is the kingdom of the heavens.
Blessed are you when they revile you and persecute you and say every kind of evil against you falsely on account of me.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward is great in the heavens; for so they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
You are the salt of the earth; but if the salt has lost its taste, with what will it be salted? It is no longer good for anything except to be thrown out and trampled underfoot by people.
You are the light of the world. A city set on a mountain cannot be hidden;
nor do they light a lamp and put it under the measuring basket, but on the lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house.
In the same way let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good works and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.
Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.

cmp.note: 「律法和先知」是当时对犹太人经书（就是基督教说的旧约）的通称：「律法」指开头的五卷，「先知」指先知们的书。
cmp.en: "The Law and the Prophets" was the usual name for the Jewish scriptures (what Christians call the Old Testament): "the Law" is the first five books, "the Prophets" the prophetic books.

verses.en: For truly I say to you, until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke will pass from the Law until all has come to pass.

cmp.note: iōta 是希腊字母里最小的一个，keraia 是字母上的一个小笔画。和合本译「一点一画」。
cmp.en: Iota is the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet, and keraia a small stroke on a letter. The Union Version has 一点一画 (yì diǎn yí huà, "one dot, one stroke").

verses.en: Therefore whoever relaxes one of the least of these commandments and teaches people so will be called least in the kingdom of the heavens; but whoever does them and teaches them, he will be called great in the kingdom of the heavens.
For I say to you that unless your righteousness goes beyond that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.
You have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘You shall not murder; and whoever murders will be liable to judgment.’

cmp.note: 从这里到本章末，耶稣六次说「你们听过有话说……可是我告诉你们」。前面引的大多是摩西律法里的话（旧约《出埃及记》20–21 章、《利未记》19 章、《申命记》24 章等）；第 43 节的「恨你的仇敌」在律法里没有原话。
cmp.en: From here to the end of the chapter Jesus says six times, "You have heard that it was said … but I say to you." What he cites is mostly from the law of Moses (Exodus 20–21, Leviticus 19, Deuteronomy 24 and elsewhere); "hate your enemy" in verse 43 is not found in the law in those words.

verses.en: But I say to you that everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment; and whoever says to his brother, ‘Raka,’ will be liable to the council; and whoever says, ‘Fool,’ will be liable to the Gehenna of fire.

cmp.note: 原文是「欣嫩谷」，耶路撒冷城南的一条山谷，后来成了恶人最后受罚之处的代称。两种中文都写「地狱」，英文照音写 Gehenna。
cmp.en: The Greek is "Gehenna," the Valley of Hinnom south of Jerusalem, which came to stand for the place where the wicked are finally punished. Both Chinese versions write 地狱 (dìyù, "hell"); the English keeps the name.

verses.en: So if you are offering your gift at the altar and there remember that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
Come to terms quickly with your accuser while you are with him on the way, lest the accuser hand you over to the judge, and the judge to the officer, and you be thrown into prison.
Truly I say to you, you will certainly not come out from there until you have paid the last penny.
You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall not commit adultery.’
But I say to you that everyone who looks at a woman so as to desire her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
And if your right eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body be thrown into Gehenna.
And if your right hand causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you; for it is better for you that one of your members perish than that your whole body go away into Gehenna.
And it was said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife, let him give her a certificate of divorce.’
But I say to you that everyone who divorces his wife, except on the ground of sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery; and whoever marries a divorced woman commits adultery.
Again you have heard that it was said to those of old, ‘You shall not break your oath, but shall perform to the Lord what you have sworn.’
But I say to you, do not swear at all: neither by heaven, for it is the throne of God;
nor by the earth, for it is the footstool of his feet; nor by Jerusalem, for it is the city of the great King.
Nor shall you swear by your head, for you cannot make one hair white or black.
But let your word be ‘Yes, yes,’ ‘No, no’; anything more than these is from the evil one.

cmp.note: 这几个字可以读成「从那恶者（魔鬼）来的」，也可以读成「从恶来的」，原文两种都说得通。和合本、白话、英文都取前一种。
cmp.en: The phrase can be read "from the evil one" (the devil) or "from evil"; the Greek allows both. Both Chinese versions and the English take the first.

verses.en: You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I say to you, do not resist the evil person; but whoever slaps you on your right cheek, turn to him the other also;
and to the one who wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well;
and whoever forces you to go one mile, go with him two.

cmp.note: 这个词指官方强征：罗马士兵可以叫路人替他背东西走一段路。原文的「里」是罗马里，约一公里半。
cmp.en: The verb refers to official requisition: a Roman soldier could make a passer-by carry his load for a distance. The "mile" is the Roman mile, about a kilometer and a half.

verses.en: Give to the one who asks you, and do not turn away from the one who wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’
But I say to you, love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
so that you may become sons of your Father who is in the heavens, for he makes his sun rise on the evil and the good, and sends rain on the just and the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not even the tax collectors do the same?
And if you greet only your brothers, what more are you doing than others? Do not even the Gentiles do the same?
You therefore shall be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.

chapters.title: Chapter 6 · The Sermon on the Mount (2): Giving, Prayer, Fasting; Do Not Worry
chapters.intro: Jesus continues: do not do good in order to be seen. Giving to the poor, praying and fasting are all to be done in secret, where the Father sees. He gives the disciples a prayer, later known as the Lord’s Prayer. Then he says to store up treasure in heaven, that no one can serve both God and money, and that they should not worry about food and clothing but seek first the kingdom and its righteousness. The whole chapter is Jesus speaking, continuing from chapter 5.

verses.en: Take care not to do your righteousness before people, in order to be seen by them; otherwise you have no reward with your Father who is in the heavens.

So when you give to the poor, do not sound a trumpet before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that they may be praised by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward.

cmp.note: 这个词原来指戏台上戴着面具的演员，引申为装样子给人看的人。和合本译「假冒为善的人」，白话写「装模作样的人」。
cmp.en: The word originally meant an actor on the stage, wearing a mask, and so someone who puts on a show for others. The Union Version has 假冒为善的人 (jiǎmào wéi shàn de rén, "those who feign goodness"); the plain Chinese writes 装模作样的人 (zhuāngmú zuòyàng de rén, "those who put on an act").

verses.en: But when you give to the poor, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing,
so that your giving may be in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.

And when you pray, you shall not be like the hypocrites; for they love to pray standing in the synagogues and on the corners of the wide streets, so that they may be seen by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you pray, go into your inner room and, having shut your door, pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
And when praying, do not babble on like the Gentiles, for they think that they will be heard for their many words.
So do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
Pray, then, in this way: ‘Our Father who is in the heavens, may your name be held holy,
may your kingdom come, may your will be done, as in heaven, so also on earth.
Give us today our daily bread;

cmp.note: 这个形容词在别的希腊文献里几乎没有出现过，意思不能确定：可以是「每天的」「今天需要的」，也可以是「明天的」。和合本译「日用的」。原文是「饼」，和合本译成「饮食」。
cmp.en: This adjective is almost unknown elsewhere in Greek and its meaning is uncertain: "daily," "needed for today," or "for tomorrow." The Union Version has 日用的 (rìyòng de, "for daily use"). The Greek noun is "bread," which the Union Version widens to 饮食 (yǐnshí, "food and drink").

verses.en: and forgive us our debts, as we also have forgiven our debtors;

cmp.note: 原文是「债」，这里指人对上帝的亏欠；第 14–15 节解释这一句时，换成了「过犯」这个词。
cmp.en: The Greek is "debts," meaning here what people owe to God; when verses 14–15 explain this line, the word changes to "trespasses."

verses.en: and do not bring us into temptation, but deliver us from the evil one.’

cmp.note: 和第 5 章第 37 节一样，这几个字可以读成「脱离那恶者（魔鬼）」，也可以读成「脱离恶」。和合本译「脱离凶恶」，白话和英文取「那恶者」。
cmp.en: As in 5:37, the phrase can be read "from the evil one" (the devil) or "from evil." The Union Version has 脱离凶恶 (tuōlí xiōng’è, "from evil"); the plain Chinese and the English take "the evil one."

verses.en: For if you forgive people their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
but if you do not forgive people, neither will your Father forgive your trespasses.
And when you fast, do not become gloomy like the hypocrites, for they disfigure their faces so that their fasting may be seen by people. Truly I say to you, they have received their reward.
But you, when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face,
so that your fasting may not be seen by people but by your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will repay you.
Do not store up for yourselves treasures on earth, where moth and rust destroy and where thieves break in and steal;
but store up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust destroys and where thieves do not break in or steal;
for where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.
The lamp of the body is the eye. If, then, your eye is single, your whole body will be full of light;

cmp.note: 字面是「单一的、单纯的」，也有「慷慨」的意思；下一节的「坏眼睛」在犹太人的说法里常指小气、贪心。和合本译成「瞭亮」和「昏花」，是照眼睛好坏来理解的。
cmp.en: Literally "single, simple," and it can also mean "generous"; the "evil eye" of the next verse was a common Jewish expression for stinginess or greed. The Union Version takes the pair as good and bad eyesight: 瞭亮 (liàoliàng, "clear") and 昏花 (hūnhuā, "dim").

verses.en: but if your eye is evil, your whole body will be full of darkness. If, then, the light that is in you is darkness, how great the darkness!
No one can serve two masters; for either he will hate the one and love the other, or he will be devoted to the one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and mammon.

cmp.note: 这是亚兰话，意思是「钱财、产业」，经文照着读音写进了希腊文。和合本也照音写「玛门」，英文写 mammon，白话译成「钱财」。
cmp.en: An Aramaic word for "wealth, property," carried into the Greek by its sound. The Union Version also writes it by sound, 玛门 (Mǎmén), and the English keeps "mammon"; the plain Chinese translates it as 钱财 (qiáncái, "money").

verses.en: Therefore I say to you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, nor about your body, what you will put on. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they do not sow or reap or gather into barns, and your heavenly Father feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they?
And which of you by worrying can add one cubit to his span of life?

cmp.w: epi tēn hēlikian autou pēchyn hena
cmp.note: 字面是「给自己的 hēlikia 加一肘」。hēlikia 可以是「寿命」，也可以是「身高」；肘是长度单位，约半米。多数人读成给寿命加一小段，和合本、白话都这样译。
cmp.en: Literally "add one cubit to his hēlikia." Hēlikia can mean "span of life" or "height"; a cubit is a measure of length, about half a meter. Most take it as adding a short stretch to one’s life, as both Chinese versions do.

verses.en: And why do you worry about clothing? Consider the lilies of the field, how they grow: they do not toil or spin;
yet I say to you that not even Solomon in all his glory was clothed like one of these.
But if God so clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, will he not much more clothe you, you of little faith?
So do not worry, saying, ‘What shall we eat?’ or ‘What shall we drink?’ or ‘What shall we wear?’
For the Gentiles seek after all these things; for your heavenly Father knows that you need them all.
But seek first the kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things will be added to you.

cmp.w: tēn basileian kai tēn dikaiosynēn autou
cmp.note: 本站的底本是「那国和他的义」，没有说是谁的国；多数抄本作「上帝的国」。白话照和合本写「他的国」，英文照底本。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "the kingdom and his righteousness," without saying whose kingdom; most manuscripts read "the kingdom of God." The Chinese follows the Union Version with 他的国 (tā de guó, "his kingdom"); the English follows the edition.

verses.en: So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself; sufficient for the day is its own trouble.

chapters.title: Chapter 7 · Do Not Judge; the Narrow Gate; Two Foundations
chapters.intro: This chapter continues the two before it: Jesus is still speaking on the mountain. Do not judge others, and look to your own faults first; ask the Father in heaven and you will receive; treat others as you want to be treated; take the narrow gate, and know false prophets by their fruit; whoever hears and acts is like a man who built his house on rock. When he finishes, the crowds are astonished at the authority with which he speaks.

verses.en: Do not judge, so that you may not be judged;
for with the judgment you judge you will be judged, and with the measure you measure it will be measured to you.
And why do you look at the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how will you say to your brother, ‘Let me take the speck out of your eye,’ and look, the beam is in your own eye?
Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
Do not give what is holy to the dogs, nor throw your pearls before the pigs, lest they trample them under their feet and turn and tear you.
Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and it will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks receives, and the one who seeks finds, and to the one who knocks it will be opened.
Or what man is there among you, whom his son will ask for bread—will he give him a stone?
Or he will also ask for a fish—will he give him a snake?
If you then, being evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father who is in the heavens give good things to those who ask him.
So everything that you want people to do to you, do so also to them; for this is the Law and the Prophets.

cmp.note: 「律法和先知」是当时对犹太经书的叫法：「律法」是摩西传下的头五卷，「先知」是各位先知的书，合起来就是今天说的旧约圣经。原文只说「这就是律法和先知」，白话的「的意思」、和合本的「的道理」都是补的。
cmp.en: "The Law and the Prophets" was the name then used for the Jewish scriptures: the Law is the five books handed down from Moses, the Prophets the books of the prophets, together what is now called the Old Testament. The Greek says only "this is the Law and the Prophets"; the plain Chinese adds 的意思 (de yìsi, "the meaning of") and the Union Version 的道理 (de dàolǐ, "the teaching of").

verses.en: Enter through the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the road that leads away to destruction, and many are those who enter through it;
for narrow is the gate and hard-pressed the road that leads away to life, and few are those who find it.
Beware of the false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
By their fruits you will recognize them. Do people gather grapes from thorns or figs from thistles?
So every good tree produces good fruit, but the rotten tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor a rotten tree produce good fruit.
Every tree not producing good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.
So then, by their fruits you will recognize them.
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of the heavens, but the one who does the will of my Father who is in the heavens.
Many will say to me on that day, ‘Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name, and in your name cast out demons, and in your name do many mighty works?’
And then I will declare to them, ‘I never knew you; depart from me, you who work lawlessness.’
Therefore everyone who hears these words of mine and does them will be like a sensible man who built his house on the rock.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and fell upon that house, and it did not fall, for it had been founded on the rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not do them will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
And the rain came down and the rivers came and the winds blew and beat against that house, and it fell, and great was its fall.”
And it happened, when Jesus finished these words, that the crowds were astonished at his teaching,

cmp.note: 从第 5 章开始的这一大段讲话到上一节结束。「耶稣讲完了这些话」这句话在这卷书里一共出现五次（另见 11:1、13:53、19:1、26:1），每次都接在一大段讲话后面。
cmp.en: The long speech that began in chapter 5 ends with the previous verse. The sentence "when Jesus finished these words" occurs five times in this book (also 11:1; 13:53; 19:1; 26:1), each time closing a long speech.

verses.en: for he was teaching them as one having authority, and not as their scribes.

chapters.title: Chapter 8 · A Leper, a Centurion’s Servant, the Storm Stilled
chapters.intro: Coming down from the mountain, Jesus heals one person after another: a man with a skin disease, the servant of a Roman centurion (whose faith he praises), Peter’s mother-in-law and many more. To those who want to follow him he says that the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head. A storm rises as they cross the lake; he rebukes the winds and the water and there is calm. On the far shore he drives demons out of two men into a herd of pigs, and the townspeople beg him to leave.

verses.en: And when he came down from the mountain, great crowds followed him.
And look, a man with a skin disease came up and was bowing down before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
And stretching out his hand he touched him, saying, “I am willing; be made clean.” And immediately his skin disease was cleansed.
And Jesus says to him, “See that you tell no one; but go, show yourself to the priest, and offer the gift that Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
And when he entered Capernaum, a centurion came up to him, begging him
and saying, “Lord, my servant is lying at home paralyzed, terribly tormented.”

cmp.note: 原文 pais 可以指「仆人」，也可以指「孩子」。这里多数译本译「仆人」，白话、英文与和合本都这样译；第 9 节的「奴仆」是另一个词（doulos）。
cmp.en: Greek pais can mean "servant" or "child." Most translations take it as "servant" here, as do both Chinese versions and the English; the "slave" of verse 9 is a different word (doulos).

verses.en: And he says to him, “I will come and heal him.”
And the centurion answered and said, “Lord, I am not fit for you to come under my roof; but only say a word, and my servant will be healed.
For I too am a man under authority, having soldiers under me; and I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
And hearing this, Jesus marveled and said to those following, “Truly I say to you, with no one in Israel have I found such faith.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「在以色列，我没有在任何人身上见过」；多数抄本是「就是在以色列，我也没有见过」，和合本跟的是后一种。意思差别不大。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "with no one in Israel have I found"; most manuscripts read "not even in Israel have I found," which the Union Version follows. The difference in sense is slight.

verses.en: And I say to you that many will come from east and west and recline at table with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of the heavens,
but the sons of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness; there will be the weeping and the grinding of teeth.”
And Jesus said to the centurion, “Go; as you have believed, let it be done for you.” And the servant was healed in that hour.
And when Jesus came into Peter’s house, he saw his mother-in-law lying down and with a fever;
and he touched her hand, and the fever left her, and she got up and began to serve him.
And when evening came, they brought to him many who were possessed by demons; and he cast out the spirits with a word, and healed all who were sick,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, “He took our weaknesses and carried our diseases.”

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《以赛亚书》53:4。「这是要应验先知某某说的话」是这卷书常用的句式，前后出现十来次。
cmp.en: The quotation is Isaiah 53:4. "So that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled" is a formula this book uses about ten times.

verses.en: Now Jesus, seeing great crowds around him, gave orders to go away to the other side.
And one scribe came up and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
And Jesus says to him, “The foxes have dens and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
And another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, permit me first to go away and bury my father.”
But Jesus says to him, “Follow me, and leave the dead to bury their own dead.”
And when he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And look, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was being covered by the waves; but he himself was sleeping.

cmp.note: 原文 seismos 字面是「震动」，平常指地震，这里指湖上的大风浪。「海」指加利利海，其实是一个大湖，所以白话写「湖」，英文照原文写 sea。
cmp.en: Greek seismos is literally "a shaking," the usual word for an earthquake; here it is a violent storm on the water. The "sea" is the Sea of Galilee, in fact a large lake, so the plain Chinese writes 湖 (hú, "lake") while the English keeps "sea."

verses.en: And they came and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us; we are perishing.”
And he says to them, “Why are you cowardly, you of little faith?” Then getting up, he rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
And the men marveled, saying, “What sort of man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?”
And when he came to the other side, to the region of the Gadarenes, two men possessed by demons met him, coming out of the tombs, so very fierce that no one was able to pass by that road.

cmp.note: 《马可福音》第 5 章讲的是同一件事，那里地名是「格拉森人的地方」，被鬼附的是一个人；这里是「加大拉人的地方」，两个人。两卷书各照各的底本译，没有改成一致。
cmp.en: Mark 5 tells the same event; there the place is "the region of the Gerasenes" and one man is possessed, while here it is "the region of the Gadarenes" and two men. Each book is translated as its own text stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And look, they cried out, saying, “What have we to do with you, Son of God? Have you come here before the time to torment us?”
Now far off from them a herd of many pigs was feeding.
And the demons were begging him, saying, “If you cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
And he said to them, “Go.” And they came out and went off into the pigs; and look, the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters.
And those feeding them fled, and going away into the town they reported everything, and what had happened to the demon-possessed men.
And look, the whole town came out to meet Jesus, and when they saw him, they begged him to move on from their borders.

chapters.title: Chapter 9 · Forgiveness, the Call of Matthew, Many Healed
chapters.intro: Back in Capernaum, Jesus forgives the sins of a paralyzed man and tells him to get up and go home. He calls Matthew, a tax collector, to follow him, eats with tax collectors and sinners, and answers challenges about whom he eats with and why his disciples do not fast. He then raises the dead daughter of a ruler and heals a woman with a flow of blood, two blind men and a mute man. The Pharisees say he drives out demons by the ruler of the demons.

verses.en: And getting into a boat, he crossed over and came to his own town.
And look, they were bringing to him a paralyzed man lying on a bed. And Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralyzed man, “Take courage, child; your sins are forgiven.”
And look, some of the scribes said within themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
And Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said, “Why do you think evil things in your hearts?
For which is easier, to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he says to the paralyzed man, “Get up, take your bed and go to your home.”
And he got up and went away to his home.
And seeing this, the crowds were afraid and glorified God, who had given such authority to human beings.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「害怕」（ephobēthēsan）；多数抄本是「惊奇」（ethaumasan），和合本的「都惊奇」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "were afraid" (ephobēthēsan); most manuscripts read "marveled" (ethaumasan), which the Union Version follows with 都惊奇 (dōu jīngqí, "were all amazed").

verses.en: And passing on from there, Jesus saw a man sitting at the tax booth, called Matthew, and he says to him, “Follow me.” And getting up, he followed him.

cmp.note: 《马可福音》2:14 讲同一件事，那里这个人叫「亚勒腓的儿子利未」。传统上认为马太和利未是同一个人，这卷书也因他得名。
cmp.en: Mark 2:14 tells the same event and calls the man "Levi the son of Alphaeus." Tradition takes Matthew and Levi to be the same person, and this book bears his name.

verses.en: And it happened, as he was reclining at table in the house, that look, many tax collectors and sinners came and were reclining with Jesus and his disciples.
And seeing this, the Pharisees were saying to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with the tax collectors and sinners?”
But hearing it, he said, “Those who are strong have no need of a doctor, but those who are sick.
But go and learn what this means: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous but sinners.”
Then the disciples of John come to him, saying, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?”
And Jesus said to them, “Can the sons of the wedding hall mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them? But days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
And no one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment; for the patch pulls away from the garment, and a worse tear results.
Nor do they put new wine into old wineskins; otherwise the skins burst, and the wine is spilled and the skins are ruined. But they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”
While he was saying these things to them, look, a ruler came and was bowing down before him, saying, “My daughter has just died; but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
And Jesus got up and was following him, and so were his disciples.
And look, a woman who had had a flow of blood for twelve years came up from behind and touched the fringe of his cloak;
for she was saying within herself, “If I only touch his cloak, I will be saved.”
But Jesus, turning and seeing her, said, “Take courage, daughter; your faith has saved you.” And the woman was saved from that hour.

cmp.note: 原文 sōzō 这个动词既是「救」，也是「治好」。第 21、22 节三次用的都是它：白话前后写「会好」「救了你」「好了」，英文三处都写 saved，和合本写「痊愈」「救了你」「痊愈」。
cmp.en: The Greek verb sōzō means both "save" and "heal." It occurs three times in verses 21 and 22: the plain Chinese renders it "get well," "saved you," "was well," the English keeps "saved" all three times, and the Union Version has 痊愈 (quányù, "recovered"), 救了你 (jiù le nǐ, "saved you"), 痊愈.

verses.en: And when Jesus came into the ruler’s house and saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion,
he was saying, “Go away, for the girl has not died but is sleeping.” And they were laughing at him.
But when the crowd had been put out, he went in and took her hand, and the girl got up.
And this report went out into all that land.
And as Jesus was passing on from there, two blind men followed him, crying out and saying, “Have mercy on us, Son of David.”
And when he had come into the house, the blind men came to him, and Jesus says to them, “Do you believe that I am able to do this?” They say to him, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes, saying, “According to your faith let it be done for you.”
And their eyes were opened. And Jesus sternly warned them, saying, “See that no one knows.”
But they went out and spread the news of him in all that land.
And as they were going out, look, they brought to him a mute man possessed by a demon.
And when the demon had been cast out, the mute man spoke. And the crowds marveled, saying, “Never was anything like this seen in Israel.”
But the Pharisees were saying, “By the ruler of the demons he casts out the demons.”
And Jesus was going around all the towns and the villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the kingdom and healing every disease and every sickness.
And seeing the crowds, he was moved with compassion for them, because they were harassed and thrown down, like sheep not having a shepherd.
Then he says to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few;
therefore ask the lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.”

chapters.title: Chapter 10 · The Twelve Sent Out
chapters.intro: Jesus gives his twelve disciples authority, the book lists their names, and he sends them out, only to the people of Israel, to announce that the kingdom of the heavens has come near and to heal and cast out demons. From verse 5 to the end of the chapter he is giving them instructions: take no money or bag for the road; persecution will come, but do not be afraid; following him will divide families, and he must come before one’s own kin; whoever receives them receives him.

verses.en: And calling his twelve disciples to him, he gave them authority over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out and to heal every disease and every sickness.
Now the names of the twelve apostles are these: first, Simon who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Cananaean, and Judas Iscariot, the one who also handed him over.

cmp.note: 原文是 Kananaios，一般认为来自亚兰话的「热心的人」，所以和合本译「奋锐党」，白话跟着写；英文照音写。「交出去」（paradous）和合本译「卖」，原文没有买卖的意思，和后面门徒「被交给议会」是同一个动词。
cmp.en: The Greek is Kananaios, generally taken to come from an Aramaic word for "zealous one"; hence the Union Version’s 奋锐党 (Fènruì dǎng, "the Zealot party"), which the plain Chinese follows, while the English keeps the sound. "Handed over" (paradous) is rendered 卖 (mài, "sold") in the Union Version; the Greek has no sense of selling, and it is the same verb used below of the disciples being "handed over" to councils.

verses.en: These twelve Jesus sent out, instructing them, saying, “Do not go off onto a road of the nations, and do not enter a town of the Samaritans;
but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
And as you go, proclaim, saying, ‘The kingdom of the heavens has come near.’
Heal the sick, raise the dead, cleanse those with skin disease, cast out demons; freely you received, freely give.
Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,
nor a bag for the road, nor two tunics, nor sandals, nor a staff; for the worker is worthy of his food.

cmp.note: 《马可福音》6:8–9 讲同一次差派，那里说可以带一根手杖、穿凉鞋；这里说鞋和手杖都不要带。两卷书各照各的原文译，没有改成一致。
cmp.en: Mark 6:8–9, telling of the same sending, allows a staff and sandals; here neither sandals nor a staff is to be taken. Each book is translated as its own text stands, without harmonizing.

verses.en: And into whatever town or village you enter, find out who in it is worthy, and stay there until you leave.
And as you enter the house, greet it;
and if the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
And whoever does not receive you or listen to your words, as you go out of that house or town, shake off the dust of your feet.
Truly I say to you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
Look, I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves; so be shrewd as the snakes and innocent as the doves.
But beware of people; for they will hand you over to councils, and in their synagogues they will flog you;
and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, as a testimony to them and to the nations.
But when they hand you over, do not worry about how or what you are to say; for what you are to say will be given to you in that hour;
for it is not you who are speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking in you.
And brother will hand over brother to death, and a father his child, and children will rise against parents and have them put to death.
And you will be hated by all because of my name. But the one who endures to the end, this one will be saved.
But when they persecute you in this town, flee to the next; for truly I say to you, you will certainly not finish the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
A disciple is not above the teacher, nor a slave above his master.

cmp.note: 这里的「学生」和别处的「门徒」是同一个词（mathētēs），本来就是「跟老师学的人」。这一节讲的是一般的道理，所以白话写「学生」，和合本也写「学生」。
cmp.en: The "student" here is the same word (mathētēs) rendered "disciple" elsewhere; it simply means one who learns from a teacher. Because this verse states a general rule, both Chinese versions write 学生 (xuéshēng, "student").

verses.en: It is enough for the disciple that he become like his teacher, and the slave like his master. If they called the master of the house Beelzebul, how much more those of his household.
So do not fear them; for nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and hidden that will not be known.
What I tell you in the darkness, say in the light; and what you hear in the ear, proclaim on the housetops.
And do not fear those who kill the body but are not able to kill the soul; but fear rather the one who is able to destroy both soul and body in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for an assarion? And not one of them will fall to the ground apart from your Father.
But even the hairs of your head are all numbered.
So do not fear; you are worth more than many sparrows.
Therefore everyone who will acknowledge me before people, I also will acknowledge him before my Father who is in the heavens;
but whoever denies me before people, I also will deny him before my Father who is in the heavens.
Do not suppose that I came to bring peace upon the earth; I did not come to bring peace but a sword.
For I came to set a man against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law;

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节的话出自旧约《弥迦书》7:6，那里是先知描述一个人人互不信任的时代。
cmp.en: The words of this verse and the next come from Micah 7:6, where the prophet describes a time when no one can trust anyone.

verses.en: and a person’s enemies will be those of his own household.
The one who loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and the one who loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me;
and whoever does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.
The one who finds his life will lose it, and the one who loses his life for my sake will find it.

cmp.note: 这里的「性命」和第 28 节的「灵魂」在原文是同一个词（psychē），它既指人的生命，也指人里面那个不随身体死去的自己。白话和英文按上下文分开译，和合本也是这样（「灵魂」「生命」）。
cmp.en: The "life" here and the "soul" of verse 28 are the same Greek word (psychē), which means both a person’s life and the self that does not die with the body. The plain Chinese and the English render it by context, as does the Union Version with 灵魂 (línghún, "soul") and 生命 (shēngmìng, "life").

verses.en: The one who receives you receives me, and the one who receives me receives the one who sent me.

The one who receives a prophet in the name of a prophet will receive a prophet’s reward, and the one who receives a righteous person in the name of a righteous person will receive a righteous person’s reward.
And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple, truly I say to you, he will certainly not lose his reward.”

chapters.title: Chapter 11 · John’s Question; Woes on the Towns; “Come to Me”
chapters.intro: From prison John the Baptist sends his disciples to ask Jesus whether he is "the one who is coming." Jesus tells them to report to John what they see, and then speaks to the crowds about who John is. He goes on to reproach the towns that saw his mighty works and did not repent. Last, he praises the Father for revealing these things to infants, and calls all who labor and are burdened to come to him for rest.

verses.en: And it happened, when Jesus finished instructing his twelve disciples, that he moved on from there to teach and proclaim in their towns.
Now John, having heard in the prison about the works of the Christ, sent word through his disciples

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「通过他的门徒」（dia）；多数抄本是「两个门徒」（dyo），和合本的「打发两个门徒去」跟的是后一种。两个词只差一个字母。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "through his disciples" (dia); most manuscripts read "two of his disciples" (dyo), which the Union Version follows with 打发两个门徒去 (dǎfa liǎng ge méntú qù, "sent two disciples"). The two words differ by one letter.

verses.en: and said to him, “Are you the one who is coming, or are we to expect another?”
And Jesus answered and said to them, “Go and report to John what you hear and see:
the blind see again and the lame walk, those with skin disease are cleansed and the deaf hear, and the dead are raised and the poor have good news proclaimed to them;

cmp.note: 这一串话呼应旧约《以赛亚书》的几处（35:5–6、61:1），那里说上帝来拯救的时候，瞎子要看见，聋子要听见，穷人要听到好消息。
cmp.en: This list echoes several places in Isaiah (35:5–6; 61:1), which say that when God comes to save, the blind will see, the deaf hear, and the poor hear good news.

verses.en: and blessed is whoever does not stumble because of me.”
And as these were going, Jesus began to say to the crowds about John, “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those wearing soft clothing are in the houses of kings.
But why did you go out? To see a prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look, I am sending my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.’

cmp.note: 引的是旧约《玛拉基书》3:1（并《出埃及记》23:20）。《马可福音》1:2 在讲约翰出场时引了同一句。
cmp.en: The quotation is Malachi 3:1 (with Exodus 23:20). Mark 1:2 quotes the same sentence when John first appears.

verses.en: Truly I say to you, among those born of women there has not arisen anyone greater than John the Baptist; yet the least in the kingdom of the heavens is greater than he.
And from the days of John the Baptist until now the kingdom of the heavens is being forced, and forceful men seize it.

cmp.note: 这一节的意思历来有两种读法。原文 biazetai 可以读成「受到暴力对待」，那么后半句是强暴的人要夺走天国，白话和英文取这一种；也可以读成「正用力推进」，那么后半句是奋力的人抓住了它，和合本的「天国是努力进入的，努力的人就得着了」取这一种。
cmp.en: This verse has long been read in two ways. Greek biazetai can be taken as "suffers violence," so that the second half speaks of violent men seizing the kingdom, which is how the plain Chinese and the English take it; or as "is forcefully advancing," so that those who press hard lay hold of it, which is how the Union Version takes it: 天国是努力进入的，努力的人就得着了 (tiānguó shì nǔlì jìnrù de, nǔlì de rén jiù dézháo le, "the kingdom of heaven is entered by effort, and those who strive obtain it").

verses.en: For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John;
and if you are willing to accept it, he himself is Elijah who is to come.

cmp.note: 旧约《玛拉基书》4:5 说，在「主的大日子」来到以前，上帝要先派先知以利亚来。耶稣这里说，约翰就是那位「要来的以利亚」。
cmp.en: Malachi 4:5 says that before "the great day of the Lord" God will first send the prophet Elijah. Jesus says here that John is that "Elijah who is to come."

verses.en: The one having ears, let him hear.
But to what shall I compare this generation? It is like children sitting in the marketplaces, who call out to the others
and say, ‘We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not beat your breasts.’
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they say, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they say, ‘Look, a glutton and a drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners.’ And wisdom is shown to be right by her works.”

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「凭它做出的事」（ergōn）；多数抄本是「凭它的儿女」（teknōn），和《路加福音》7:35 一样，和合本的「智慧之子，总以智慧为是」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "by her works" (ergōn); most manuscripts read "by her children" (teknōn), as in Luke 7:35, which the Union Version follows with 智慧之子，总以智慧为是 (zhìhuì zhī zǐ, zǒng yǐ zhìhuì wéi shì, "the children of wisdom always hold wisdom to be right").

verses.en: Then he began to reproach the towns in which most of his mighty works had been done, because they did not repent:
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
Nevertheless I say to you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be exalted to heaven? You will go down to Hades. For if the mighty works done in you had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until today.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是一句问话：「你难道要被高举到天上吗？」多数抄本是一句陈述：「你这被高举到天上的」，和合本的「你已经升到天上」跟的是后一种。这句话呼应旧约《以赛亚书》14:13–15。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows has a question: "will you be exalted to heaven?" Most manuscripts have a statement, "you who have been exalted to heaven," which the Union Version follows with 你已经升到天上 (nǐ yǐjīng shēng dào tiānshàng, "you have already risen to heaven"). The saying echoes Isaiah 14:13–15.

verses.en: Nevertheless I say to you that it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom on the day of judgment than for you.”
At that time Jesus answered and said, “I praise you, Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that you hid these things from the wise and understanding and revealed them to infants;
yes, Father, for such was your good pleasure.
All things have been handed over to me by my Father, and no one knows the Son except the Father, nor does anyone know the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to reveal him.
Come to me, all who labor and are heavily burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, for I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls;
for my yoke is easy and my burden is light.”

chapters.title: Chapter 12 · Sabbath Disputes; Beelzebul; the Sign of Jonah
chapters.intro: Twice the Pharisees fault Jesus over the Sabbath: his disciples pluck grain, and he heals a withered hand. They begin to plan how to destroy him. When he drives out a demon, the Pharisees say he does it by Beelzebul, ruler of the demons; he answers them and says that blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven. Asked for a sign, he offers only the sign of Jonah. At the end he says that whoever does the will of his Father is his true family.

verses.en: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath; and his disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
But the Pharisees, seeing it, said to him, “Look, your disciples are doing what is not permitted to do on a Sabbath.”
But he said to them, “Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, and those with him:
how he entered the house of God and they ate the loaves of the presentation, which it was not permitted for him to eat nor for those with him, but for the priests alone?
Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbaths the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and are guiltless?
But I say to you that something greater than the temple is here.
But if you had known what this means, ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice,’ you would not have condemned the guiltless.
For the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.”
And moving on from there, he came into their synagogue;
and look, a man having a withered hand. And they questioned him, saying, “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbaths?”—so that they might accuse him.
But he said to them, “What man will there be among you who will have one sheep, and if this one falls into a pit on the Sabbaths, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much more valuable then is a person than a sheep. So it is permitted to do good on the Sabbaths.”
Then he says to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” And he stretched it out, and it was restored, healthy like the other.
But the Pharisees went out and took counsel against him, how they might destroy him.
But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from there. And many followed him, and he healed them all,
and he warned them not to make him known,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, saying:
“Look, my servant whom I have chosen, my beloved in whom my soul is well pleased; I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will announce justice to the nations.

cmp.note: 第 18–21 节引的是旧约《以赛亚书》42:1–4，是这卷书里最长的一段引文。措辞和今天通行的旧约本子不完全一样。
cmp.en: Verses 18–21 quote Isaiah 42:1–4, the longest quotation in this book. The wording does not match the standard Old Testament text exactly.

verses.en: He will not quarrel nor cry out, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.
A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not quench, until he brings justice out to victory.
And in his name the nations will hope.”
Then a demon-possessed man, blind and mute, was brought to him; and he healed him, so that the mute man spoke and saw.
And all the crowds were amazed and were saying, “Could this be the Son of David?”
But the Pharisees, hearing it, said, “This man does not cast out the demons except by Beelzebul, ruler of the demons.”
But knowing their thoughts, he said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and every town or house divided against itself will not stand.
And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself; how then will his kingdom stand?
And if I cast out the demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out the demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

cmp.note: 这卷书平常说「天国」（字面是「诸天的国」），这里却说「上帝的国」，全书只有四五处这样写。一般认为两个说法指的是同一件事。
cmp.en: This book normally says "the kingdom of the heavens"; here it says "the kingdom of God," one of only four or five places in the book that do. The two phrases are generally taken to mean the same thing.

verses.en: Or how can anyone enter the house of the strong man and carry off his goods, unless he first binds the strong man? And then he will plunder his house.
The one who is not with me is against me, and the one who does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I say to you, every sin and blasphemy will be forgiven people, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.
And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man, it will be forgiven him; but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit, it will not be forgiven him, neither in this age nor in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree rotten and its fruit rotten; for by the fruit the tree is known.
Offspring of vipers, how can you speak good things, being evil? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.
The good person out of the good treasure brings out good things, and the evil person out of the evil treasure brings out evil things.
But I say to you that every idle word that people will speak, they will give account for it on the day of judgment;
for by your words you will be declared righteous, and by your words you will be condemned.”
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
But he answered and said to them, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

cmp.note: 约拿的故事在旧约《约拿书》：上帝派他去外族的大城尼尼微宣讲，他不肯去，坐船逃走，被一条大鱼吞下，在鱼肚子里三天三夜；后来他去了，尼尼微人听了就悔改。
cmp.en: The story of Jonah is in the Old Testament book of Jonah: God sends him to preach in the great foreign city of Nineveh; he refuses and flees by ship, is swallowed by a great fish and spends three days and three nights in its belly; when he does go, the people of Nineveh hear him and repent.

verses.en: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.
The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

The queen of the south will be raised at the judgment with this generation and will condemn it, for she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and look, something greater than Solomon is here.

cmp.note: 「南方的女王」指旧约《列王纪上》第 10 章的示巴女王，她远道来到耶路撒冷，试问所罗门王的智慧。
cmp.en: "The queen of the south" is the queen of Sheba in 1 Kings 10, who traveled a great distance to Jerusalem to test the wisdom of King Solomon.

verses.en: Now when the unclean spirit goes out of the person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest, and does not find it.
Then it says, ‘I will return to my house from which I came out’; and coming, it finds it unoccupied, swept and put in order.

Then it goes and takes along with itself seven other spirits more evil than itself, and entering they dwell there; and the last state of that person becomes worse than the first. So it will be also with this evil generation.”
While he was still speaking to the crowds, look, his mother and brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to him.
And someone said to him, “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you.”
But he answered and said to the one telling him, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said, “Here are my mother and my brothers!
For whoever does the will of my Father who is in the heavens, this one is my brother and sister and mother.”

chapters.title: Chapter 13 · Seven Parables of the Kingdom; Rejected at Home
chapters.intro: From a boat Jesus speaks to the crowd on the shore in parables: the sower, the weeds among the wheat, the mustard seed, the leaven. Asked by the disciples why he uses parables, he answers with words of Isaiah, and in private he explains the sower and the weeds. He adds three more: the hidden treasure, the pearl, the dragnet. Then he goes to his hometown, where the people will not accept him.

verses.en: On that day Jesus went out of the house and was sitting beside the sea.
And large crowds gathered to him, so that he got into a boat and sat down, and the whole crowd stood on the shore.
And he spoke many things to them in parables, saying, “Look, the sower went out to sow.
And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, and the birds came and ate them up.
And others fell on the rocky places where they did not have much soil, and immediately they sprang up, because they had no depth of soil;
and when the sun rose they were scorched, and because they had no root they withered.
And others fell upon the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them.
And others fell upon the good soil and were giving fruit, some a hundredfold, some sixty, some thirty.
Whoever has ears, let him hear.”
And the disciples came and said to him, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
And answering he said to them, “Because to you it has been given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, but to those it has not been given.
For whoever has, to him it will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.
For this reason I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand.

cmp.note: 这里的连接词是「因为」（hoti）：用比喻，是因为他们看了也看不见。《马可福音》4:12 同一处用的是「为的是」（hina），两卷书的说法不一样。
cmp.en: The connective here is "because" (hoti): he uses parables because they see without seeing. At the same point Mark 4:12 has "so that" (hina); the two books put it differently.

verses.en: And in them is fulfilled the prophecy of Isaiah that says, ‘With hearing you will hear and never understand, and seeing you will see and never perceive.

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引的是旧约《以赛亚书》6:9–10，那里是上帝对先知以赛亚说的话，讲百姓听了也不肯明白。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Isaiah 6:9–10, where God is speaking to the prophet Isaiah about a people who hear and will not understand.

verses.en: For the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have heard with difficulty, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears and understand with their heart and turn back, and I would heal them.’
But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
For truly I say to you that many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see and did not see it, and to hear what you hear and did not hear it.
You then, hear the parable of the sower.
When anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart; this is the one sown beside the road.
And the one sown on the rocky places, this is the one who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy,
yet he has no root in himself but lasts only for a time, and when affliction or persecution comes because of the word, immediately he stumbles.
And the one sown among the thorns, this is the one who hears the word, and the care of this age and the deceit of wealth choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
And the one sown on the good soil, this is the one who hears the word and understands it, who indeed bears fruit and yields, one a hundredfold, one sixty, one thirty.”
He put another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of the heavens has become like a man who sowed good seed in his field.
But while people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds in among the wheat and went away.

cmp.note: 原文 zizania 指一种麦田里的杂草（一般认为是毒麦），没有抽穗以前和麦子很难分清。和合本译「稗子」，白话沿用。
cmp.en: Greek zizania is a weed of grain fields (generally taken to be darnel) that is hard to tell from wheat until the ears form. The Union Version has 稗子 (bàizi, "barnyard grass"), which the plain Chinese keeps.

verses.en: And when the plants sprouted and bore grain, then the weeds appeared also.
And the slaves of the master of the house came and said to him, ‘Master, did you not sow good seed in your field? Where then does it have weeds from?’
And he said to them, ‘An enemy has done this.’ And the slaves say to him, ‘Do you then want us to go and gather them?’
But he says, ‘No, lest while gathering the weeds you uproot the wheat along with them.
Let both grow together until the harvest; and at harvest time I will say to the reapers, Gather the weeds first and bind them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my barn.’”
He put another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of the heavens is like a mustard seed, which a man took and sowed in his field;
it is smaller than all the seeds, but when it has grown it is greater than the garden plants and becomes a tree, so that the birds of the sky come and nest in its branches.”
He spoke another parable to them: “The kingdom of the heavens is like leaven, which a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until it was all leavened.”

cmp.note: 「斗」原文是 saton，一种量干粮的单位；三个 saton 合起来约四十升面粉，是很大的一团面。和合本写「三斗」，白话沿用。
cmp.en: The measure is the saton, a unit for dry goods; three of them come to roughly forty litres of flour, a very large batch of dough. The Union Version writes 三斗 (sān dǒu, "three pecks"), which the plain Chinese keeps.

verses.en: All these things Jesus spoke to the crowds in parables, and without a parable he was speaking nothing to them,
so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying, “I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things hidden since the foundation.”

cmp.note: 这句话引自旧约《诗篇》78:2。本站的底本只写「从奠基以来」（apo katabolēs），没有「世界」一词；许多抄本作「从世界奠基以来」，和合本的「创世以来」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The words come from Psalm 78:2. The edition this site follows has only "since the foundation" (apo katabolēs), without "of the world"; many manuscripts add it, and the Union Version follows them with 创世以来 (chuàngshì yǐlái, "since the creation of the world").

verses.en: Then leaving the crowds he came into the house. And his disciples came to him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds of the field.”
And answering he said, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man;
and the field is the world; and the good seed, these are the sons of the kingdom; and the weeds are the sons of the evil one,

cmp.note: 字面是「国的儿子们」「那恶者的儿子们」。「某某的儿子」是从希伯来话来的说法，意思是「属于某某的人」。和合本译「天国之子」「恶者之子」。
cmp.en: Literally "the sons of the kingdom" and "the sons of the evil one." "Son of X" is a turn of phrase carried over from Hebrew, meaning "one who belongs to X." The Union Version has 天国之子 (tiānguó zhī zǐ, "sons of the kingdom of heaven") and 恶者之子 (èzhě zhī zǐ, "sons of the evil one").

verses.en: and the enemy who sowed them is the devil; and the harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are angels.
Just as the weeds, then, are gathered and burned with fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all the causes of stumbling and those who do lawlessness,
and they will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Then the righteous will shine out like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Whoever has ears, let him hear.
The kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hidden in the field, which a man found and hid; and from his joy he goes and sells all that he has and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant searching for fine pearls;
and having found one pearl of great price, he went away and sold all that he had and bought it.
Again, the kingdom of the heavens is like a dragnet thrown into the sea and gathering in of every kind,
which, when it was filled, they pulled up on the shore, and sitting down they gathered the good into containers, but the bad they threw out.
So it will be at the end of the age: the angels will go out and separate the evil from among the righteous
and will throw them into the furnace of fire; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.
Have you understood all these things?” They say to him, “Yes.”
And he said to them, “For this reason every scribe who has been made a disciple for the kingdom of the heavens is like a man, a master of a house, who brings out of his treasure things new and old.”
And it happened, when Jesus had finished these parables, that he went away from there.
And coming into his hometown he was teaching them in their synagogue, so that they were astonished and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these mighty works?
Is this not the carpenter’s son? Is not his mother called Mary, and his brothers James and Joseph and Simon and Judas?

cmp.note: 本站的底本这里是「约瑟」（Iōsēph）；另一些抄本是「约西」（Iōsēs），和《马可福音》6:3 一样，和合本跟的是后一种。两个名字本来是同一个名字的两种叫法。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "Joseph" (Iōsēph); other manuscripts read "Joses" (Iōsēs), as in Mark 6:3, and the Union Version follows them with 约西 (Yuēxī, "Joses"). The two are forms of the same name.

verses.en: And his sisters, are they not all here with us? Where then did this man get all these things?”
And they were taking offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown and in his own house.”
And he did not do many mighty works there, because of their unbelief.

chapters.title: Chapter 14 · John Beheaded; Five Loaves and Two Fish; Walking on the Sea
chapters.intro: Herod the tetrarch hears about Jesus and takes him for John the Baptist, whom he had killed, come back to life; the book then tells how John was beheaded because of an oath.
