Jesus withdraws to a deserted place and feeds more than five thousand people with five loaves and two fish. In the night he walks across the sea to the disciples’ boat; Peter steps out onto the water too, takes fright and begins to sink.

verses.en: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the report about Jesus,

cmp.note: 原文的头衔是「四分之一的统治者」：罗马把一个王国分成几块，交给几个人各管一块，希律管的是加利利一带。他的地位比王低，第 9 节却顺口叫他「王」。
cmp.en: The title means "ruler of a fourth part": Rome divided a kingdom into several pieces and gave each to a different ruler, and this Herod held the region around Galilee. He ranked below a king, though verse 9 loosely calls him "the king."

verses.en: and said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist; he has been raised from the dead, and for this reason the powers are at work in him.”
For Herod had seized John and bound him and put him away in prison because of Herodias, the wife of Philip his brother,
for John had been saying to him, “It is not lawful for you to have her.”
And though wanting to kill him, he feared the crowd, because they held him to be a prophet.
But when Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced in their midst and pleased Herod,
so that he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked.
And she, prompted by her mother, says, “Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist.”
And the king was grieved, but because of the oaths and those reclining with him he commanded it to be given,
and he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
And his head was brought on a platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
And his disciples came and took away the corpse and buried him, and they went and told Jesus.
And when Jesus heard, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by himself; and when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.
And coming out he saw a large crowd, and he had compassion on them and healed their sick.

And when evening came, the disciples came to him, saying, “The place is deserted, and the hour has already passed; send the crowds away, so that they may go into the villages and buy themselves food.”
But Jesus said to them, “They have no need to go away; you give them something to eat.”
And they say to him, “We have nothing here except five loaves and two fish.”
And he said, “Bring them here to me.”

And having commanded the crowds to recline on the grass, taking the five loaves and the two fish, looking up to heaven he blessed, and breaking the loaves he gave them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
And they all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, twelve baskets full.
And those who ate were about five thousand men, apart from women and children.
And immediately he made the disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other side, while he sent the crowds away.
And having sent the crowds away, he went up on the mountain by himself to pray. And when evening came, he was there alone.
But the boat was already many stadia away from the land, battered by the waves, for the wind was against them.

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「离岸已经好多个斯他町」（一个斯他町约一百八十五米）；另一些抄本是「在海中央」，和合本的「在海中」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "already many stadia from the land" (a stadion is about 185 metres); other manuscripts read "in the middle of the sea," which the Union Version follows with 在海中 (zài hǎi zhōng, "in the midst of the sea").

verses.en: And in the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea.
But when the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified, saying, “It is a ghost!” And they cried out from fear.
But immediately Jesus spoke to them, saying, “Take courage; it is I; do not be afraid.”
And answering him Peter said, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the waters.”
And he said, “Come.” And getting down from the boat, Peter walked on the waters and came toward Jesus.
But seeing the strong wind he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, saying, “Lord, save me!”
And immediately Jesus, stretching out his hand, took hold of him and says to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
And when they got up into the boat, the wind dropped.
And those in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly you are God’s Son.”
And having crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret.
And when the men of that place recognized him, they sent into all that surrounding region, and they brought to him all who were sick,
and they were begging him that they might only touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched it were made completely well.

cmp.note: 按旧约《民数记》15:38 的吩咐，犹太男子在外衣的四角缝上穗子，提醒自己记住上帝的诫命。和合本译「繸子」。
cmp.en: By the command in Numbers 15:38, Jewish men wore tassels on the four corners of their outer garment as a reminder of God’s commandments. The Union Version has 繸子 (suìzi, "tassels").

chapters.title: Chapter 15 · What Defiles a Person; the Canaanite Woman; Seven Loaves
chapters.intro: Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem ask Jesus why his disciples eat without washing their hands. He asks in turn why they cancel the word of God with their own tradition, and says that what defiles a person is what comes out of the heart. In the region of Tyre and Sidon he heals the daughter of a foreign woman; back beside the sea he feeds more than four thousand people with seven loaves.

verses.en: Then Pharisees and scribes come to Jesus from Jerusalem, saying,
“Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.”
And answering he said to them, “And why do you transgress the commandment of God for the sake of your tradition?
For God said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’

cmp.note: 两句话引自旧约《出埃及记》20:12 和 21:17。《马可福音》7:10 同一处说的是「摩西说过」，这里说「上帝说过」。
cmp.en: The two sayings come from Exodus 20:12 and 21:17. At the same point Mark 7:10 has "Moses said"; here it is "God said."

verses.en: But you say, ‘Whoever says to his father or mother, Whatever you would have gained from me is a gift,
he shall certainly not honor his father.’ And you have made void the word of God for the sake of your tradition.

cmp.note: 本站的底本这一节只说「父亲」，后半句是「上帝的话」；另一些抄本作「父亲或母亲」和「上帝的诫命」，和合本的「父母」「诫命」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows has only "his father" here and "the word of God" in the second half; other manuscripts read "his father or his mother" and "the commandment of God," which the Union Version follows with 父母 (fùmǔ, "father and mother") and 诫命 (jièmìng, "commandment").

verses.en: Hypocrites! Isaiah prophesied well about you, saying,
‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far away from me;

cmp.note: 这一节和下一节引自旧约《以赛亚书》29:13。
cmp.en: This verse and the next quote Isaiah 29:13.

verses.en: in vain do they worship me, teaching as teachings the commandments of men.’”
And calling the crowd to him he said to them, “Hear and understand:
it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles the person, but what comes out of the mouth, this defiles the person.”
Then the disciples came and say to him, “Do you know that the Pharisees took offense when they heard this word?”
But answering he said, “Every plant that my heavenly Father did not plant will be uprooted.
Leave them; they are blind guides of the blind; and if a blind person guides a blind person, both will fall into a pit.”
And answering, Peter said to him, “Explain this parable to us.”
And he said, “Are you also still without understanding?
Do you not see that everything that goes into the mouth passes into the stomach and is thrown out into the latrine?
But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and those defile the person.
For out of the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immoralities, thefts, false witnesses, slanders.
These are the things that defile the person; but to eat with unwashed hands does not defile the person.”
And going out from there Jesus withdrew into the region of Tyre and Sidon.
And look, a Canaanite woman from those borders came out and was crying, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David; my daughter is badly demon-possessed.”

cmp.note: 「迦南人」是旧约里对这一带原住民的老叫法。《马可福音》7:26 说的是同一个妇人，用的是当时的叫法：「希腊人，按出身是叙利非尼基人」。
cmp.en: "Canaanite" is the old name the Old Testament uses for the original peoples of this region. Mark 7:26 describes the same woman in the terms of the day: "a Greek, a Syrophoenician by birth."

verses.en: But he did not answer her a word. And his disciples came and were asking him, saying, “Send her away, for she is crying out after us.”
But answering he said, “I was not sent except to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
But she came and was bowing down before him, saying, “Lord, help me.”
But answering he said, “It is not good to take the children’s bread and throw it to the little dogs.”
But she said, “Yes, Lord, for even the little dogs eat from the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
Then answering Jesus said to her, “O woman, great is your faith; let it be done for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
And passing on from there Jesus came beside the Sea of Galilee, and going up on the mountain he was sitting there.
And large crowds came to him, having with them the mute, the blind, the lame, the crippled, and many others, and they laid them at his feet, and he healed them,
so that the crowd marveled, seeing the mute speaking, the crippled whole, and the lame walking, and the blind seeing; and they glorified the God of Israel.

And Jesus, calling his disciples to him, said, “I have compassion on the crowd, because they have stayed with me three days already and have nothing to eat; and I do not want to send them away hungry, lest they faint on the way.”
And the disciples say to him, “Where in a wilderness would we get so many loaves as to fill so great a crowd?”
And Jesus says to them, “How many loaves do you have?” And they said, “Seven, and a few small fish.”
And having ordered the crowd to recline on the ground,
he took the seven loaves and the fish, and having given thanks he broke them and was giving them to the disciples, and the disciples to the crowds.
And they all ate and were filled, and they took up what was left over of the broken pieces, seven large baskets full.
And those who ate were four thousand men, apart from women and children.
And having sent the crowds away, he got into the boat and came into the borders of Magadan.

chapters.title: Chapter 16 · Peter’s Confession; the First Passion Prediction
chapters.intro: Pharisees and Sadducees ask Jesus for a sign from heaven, and he refuses. He warns the disciples against the “leaven” of these two groups; at first they think he is talking about bread. Near Caesarea Philippi Peter says that Jesus is the Christ, and Jesus says he will build his church on this rock. From then on Jesus foretells that in Jerusalem he will suffer, be killed, and be raised on the third day.

verses.en: And the Pharisees and Sadducees came, and testing him they asked him to show them a sign from heaven.
But answering he said to them, “When evening comes you say, ‘Fair weather, for the sky is red’;

cmp.note: 从「傍晚的时候」到下一节末尾这段讲看天色的话，有几份最早的抄本没有；本站的底本和和合本都收了。
cmp.en: The saying about reading the sky, from "When evening comes" to the end of the next verse, is missing from several of the earliest manuscripts; both the edition this site follows and the Union Version include it.

verses.en: and in the morning, ‘Stormy today, for the sky is red and gloomy.’ You know how to discern the face of the sky, but the signs of the times you cannot.
An evil and adulterous generation seeks for a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.” And leaving them he went away.

cmp.note: 「约拿的神迹」在这卷书前面（12:39–40）说过：旧约《约拿书》讲先知约拿在大鱼肚子里三天三夜，耶稣说人子也要这样在地里头三天三夜。
cmp.en: The "sign of Jonah" was explained earlier in this book (12:39–40): the book of Jonah tells how the prophet was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, and Jesus says the Son of Man will likewise be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.

verses.en: And when the disciples came to the other side, they had forgotten to take loaves.
And Jesus said to them, “Watch out and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
And they were discussing among themselves, saying, “We did not take loaves.”
But knowing it Jesus said, “Why are you discussing among yourselves, you of little faith, that you have no loaves?
Do you not yet understand, nor remember the five loaves of the five thousand and how many baskets you took up?
Nor the seven loaves of the four thousand and how many large baskets you took up?
How do you not understand that I did not speak to you about loaves? But beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
Then they understood that he did not say to beware of the leaven of the loaves, but of the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
And when Jesus came into the region of Caesarea Philippi, he was asking his disciples, saying, “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?”
And they said, “Some, John the Baptist; and others, Elijah; and others, Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He says to them, “But you, who do you say that I am?”
And answering Simon Peter said, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
And answering Jesus said to him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal it to you, but my Father who is in the heavens.

cmp.note: 原文照亚兰话的读音写作 Bariōna，意思是「约拿的儿子」；和合本音译成「巴约拿」，白话译出了意思。
cmp.en: The Greek keeps the Aramaic sound, Bariōna, meaning "son of Jonah." The Union Version transliterates it as 巴约拿 (Bā Yuēná, "Bar-Jonah"); the plain Chinese gives the meaning.

verses.en: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not overpower it.

cmp.note: 「彼得」（Petros）这个名字的意思是「石头」，「磐石」原文是 petra，两个词是一对；中文和英文都看不出这层关系。「这磐石」指什么，历来各教会的理解不一样，本站不作判断。
cmp.en: The name "Peter" (Petros) means "stone," and "rock" is petra; the two words are a pair, which neither the Chinese nor the English can show. What "this rock" refers to has long been understood differently by different churches, and this site takes no position.

cmp.note: 原文是「阴间的门」。阴间（hadēs）是死人去的地方，不等于受罚的地狱。和合本译「阴间的权柄」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "the gates of Hades." Hades is the place of the dead, not the same as the hell of punishment. The Union Version has 阴间的权柄 (yīnjiān de quánbǐng, "the powers of the underworld").

verses.en: I will give you the keys of the kingdom of the heavens, and whatever you bind on the earth will have been bound in the heavens, and whatever you loose on the earth will have been loosed in the heavens.”

cmp.note: 原文的时态是「将是已经被捆绑了的」，英文照字面译；和合本写「在天上也要捆绑」。「捆绑」和「释放」是当时犹太教师的用语，一般认为指「禁止」和「准许」。
cmp.en: The Greek tense is "will be (something) having been bound," which the English keeps; the Union Version has 在天上也要捆绑 (zài tiānshàng yě yào kǔnbǎng, "will also be bound in heaven"). "Bind" and "loose" were terms used by Jewish teachers of the time, generally understood as "forbid" and "permit."

verses.en: Then he strictly charged the disciples that they should tell no one that he was the Christ.
From then Jesus began to show his disciples that he must go away to Jerusalem and suffer many things from the elders and chief priests and scribes, and be killed, and on the third day be raised.
And taking him aside Peter began to rebuke him, saying, “Mercy on you, Lord! This shall never happen to you.”
But turning he said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, for you are not thinking the things of God but the things of men.”
Then Jesus said to his disciples, “If anyone wants to come after me, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.
For what will a person be profited if he gains the whole world but forfeits his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man is about to come in the glory of his Father with his angels, and then he will repay each one according to his doing.
Truly I say to you that there are some of those standing here who will certainly not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”

chapters.title: Chapter 17 · The Transfiguration; the Boy Healed; the Temple Tax
chapters.intro: Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain and is transfigured before them; Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice from a cloud says, “This is my beloved Son.” Back down, he heals a boy the disciples could not heal and says it was because of their little faith. He foretells a second time that he will be killed and raised on the third day, and sends Peter to find a coin in a fish’s mouth to pay the temple tax.

verses.en: And after six days Jesus takes Peter and James and John his brother, and brings them up a high mountain privately.
And he was transfigured before them, and his face shone like the sun, and his garments became white as the light.
And look, Moses and Elijah appeared to them, talking with him.
And answering Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here; if you wish, I will make three tents here, one for you and one for Moses and one for Elijah.”
While he was still speaking, look, a bright cloud overshadowed them, and look, a voice out of the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; listen to him.”
And when the disciples heard, they fell on their faces and were greatly afraid.
And Jesus came and, touching them, said, “Rise, and do not be afraid.”
And lifting up their eyes they saw no one except Jesus himself alone.
And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus commanded them, saying, “Tell the vision to no one until the Son of Man has been raised from the dead.”
And the disciples asked him, saying, “Why then do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”

cmp.note: 这个说法出自旧约《玛拉基书》4:5：上帝说，在「主的大日子」来到以前，要先派先知以利亚来。
cmp.en: The saying goes back to Malachi 4:5, where God says he will send the prophet Elijah before "the great day of the Lord" comes.

verses.en: And answering he said, “Elijah does come and will restore all things;
but I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him but did to him whatever they wished. So also the Son of Man is about to suffer at their hands.”
Then the disciples understood that he spoke to them about John the Baptist.
And when they came to the crowd, a man came to him, kneeling before him
and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, for he is moonstruck and suffers badly; for often he falls into the fire and often into the water.

cmp.note: 字面是「被月亮击中」：古时候的人认为这种突然倒地抽搐的病和月亮有关。和合本和白话按病症译成「癫痫」，英文照字面。
cmp.en: Literally "is moonstruck": people in antiquity connected this illness, with its sudden falls and convulsions, with the moon. Both Chinese versions name the condition, 癫痫 (diānxián, "epilepsy"); the English keeps the literal word.

verses.en: And I brought him to your disciples, and they were not able to heal him.”
And answering Jesus said, “O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you? How long shall I bear with you? Bring him here to me.”
And Jesus rebuked it, and the demon came out of him, and the boy was healed from that hour.
Then the disciples, coming to Jesus privately, said, “Why were we not able to cast it out?”

And he says to them, “Because of your little faith; for truly I say to you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move, and nothing will be impossible for you.”

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「信心小」（oligopistia）；另一些抄本是「不信」（apistia）。和合本的「信心小」和底本一致。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "little faith" (oligopistia); other manuscripts read "unbelief" (apistia). The Union Version, with 信心小 (xìnxīn xiǎo, "small faith"), agrees with this edition.

verses.en: (This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本这里有一句话，意思是：这一类的鬼，不靠祷告和禁食就赶不出去。和合本的正文里有这一节。最早的几份抄本没有，一般认为是抄写的人照《马可福音》9:29 补进来的，所以底本不收。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning: this kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting. The Union Version prints it in its text. The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it is generally thought that copyists added it from Mark 9:29, so the edition leaves it out.

verses.en: And as they were gathering together in Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man is about to be handed over into the hands of men,

cmp.note: 本站的底本是「聚在一起」（systrephomenōn）；另一些抄本是「来往、居住」（anastrephomenōn），和合本的「还住在」跟的是后一种。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "gathering together" (systrephomenōn); other manuscripts read "going about, staying" (anastrephomenōn), which the Union Version follows with 还住在 (hái zhù zài, "were still staying in").

verses.en: and they will kill him, and on the third day he will be raised.” And they were greatly grieved.
And when they came to Capernaum, those who collect the two-drachma tax came to Peter and said, “Does your teacher not pay the two-drachma tax?”

cmp.note: 原文是「两个德拉克马」，一种希腊银币的面额，约合两天的工钱；当时每个成年犹太男子每年要交这么多钱给耶路撒冷的圣殿。和合本译「丁税」，白话写「殿税」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "the two drachmas," a Greek silver denomination worth about two days’ wages; every adult Jewish man paid this amount each year to the temple in Jerusalem. The Union Version has 丁税 (dīngshuì, "poll tax"); the plain Chinese writes 殿税 (diànshuì, "temple tax").

verses.en: He says, “Yes.” And when he came into the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth take tolls or poll tax? From their sons or from others?”
And when he said, “From others,” Jesus said to him, “Then the sons are free.

But so that we do not give them offense, go to the sea and cast a hook, and take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth you will find a stater; take that and give it to them for me and you.”

cmp.note: 原文是「一个斯他特」，一种值四个德拉克马的银币，正好够两个人的殿税。和合本译「一块钱」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "a stater," a silver coin worth four drachmas, exactly the tax for two people. The Union Version has 一块钱 (yí kuài qián, "a piece of money").

chapters.title: Chapter 18 · Who Is Greatest; the Straying Sheep; Forgiving a Brother
chapters.intro: The disciples ask who is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens. Jesus sets a little child among them and says they must become like children to enter it, warns against making the little ones stumble, and speaks of a man who goes after one straying sheep. He lays out, step by step, what to do when a brother sins against you. Peter asks how many times to forgive, and Jesus tells of a slave who was forgiven a vast debt and would not forgive a small one.

verses.en: At that hour the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Who then is greatest in the kingdom of the heavens?”
And calling a little child to him, he set him in the midst of them
and said, “Truly I say to you, unless you turn and become like little children, you will certainly not enter the kingdom of the heavens.
Whoever therefore will humble himself like this little child, this one is the greatest in the kingdom of the heavens;
and whoever receives one such little child in my name receives me.
But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble, it is better for him that a great millstone be hung around his neck and he be drowned in the depth of the sea.
Woe to the world because of the causes of stumbling! For it is necessary that the causes of stumbling come, but woe to the person through whom the cause of stumbling comes!

And if your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it from you; it is better for you to enter into life maimed or lame than, having two hands or two feet, to be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to stumble, tear it out and throw it from you; it is better for you to enter into life one-eyed than, having two eyes, to be thrown into the Gehenna of fire.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones, for I say to you that their angels in the heavens always see the face of my Father who is in the heavens.
(This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本这里有一句话，意思是：人子来，是要拯救失丧的人。最早的几份抄本没有这一句，一般认为是抄写的人照《路加福音》19:10 补进来的，所以底本不收。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have a sentence here meaning: the Son of Man came to save what was lost. The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it is generally thought that copyists added it from Luke 19:10, so the edition leaves it out.

verses.en: What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them has gone astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine on the mountains and go and seek the one that is straying?
And if it happens that he finds it, truly I say to you that he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that have not gone astray.
So it is not the will before your Father who is in the heavens that one of these little ones should perish.
And if your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained your brother;
but if he does not listen, take with you one or two more, so that ‘on the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established’;

cmp.note: 单引号里的话引自旧约《申命记》19:15：定一个人的罪，不能只凭一个人作证，要有两三个证人。
cmp.en: The words in single quotation marks come from Deuteronomy 19:15: a charge is not to stand on one person’s testimony but needs two or three witnesses.

verses.en: and if he refuses to listen to them, tell it to the church; and if he refuses to listen even to the church, let him be to you like the Gentile and the tax collector.
Truly I say to you, whatever you bind on the earth will have been bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on the earth will have been loosed in heaven.

cmp.note: 这句话在第 16 章第 19 节对彼得一个人说过，这里是对门徒大家说的（「你们」）。「捆绑」和「释放」一般认为指「禁止」和「准许」。
cmp.en: The same saying was addressed to Peter alone in 16:19; here it is said to the disciples as a group ("you" is plural). "Bind" and "loose" are generally understood as "forbid" and "permit."

verses.en: Again, truly I say to you that if two of you agree on the earth about any matter that they ask, it will be done for them by my Father who is in the heavens.
For where two or three are gathered in my name, there I am in the midst of them.”
Then Peter came and said to him, “Lord, how often will my brother sin against me and I forgive him? Up to seven times?”
Jesus says to him, “I do not say to you up to seven times, but up to seventy-seven times.

cmp.note: 原文可以读成「七十七次」，也可以读成「七十个七次」（四百九十次）；白话和英文取前一种，和合本取后一种。两种读法的意思一样：不要去数。
cmp.en: The Greek can be read as "seventy-seven times" or as "seventy times seven" (four hundred and ninety); the plain Chinese and the English take the first, the Union Version the second with 七十个七次 (qīshí gè qī cì, "seventy sevens of times"). Either way the point is the same: do not keep count.

verses.en: For this reason the kingdom of the heavens has become like a man, a king, who wished to settle accounts with his slaves.
And when he began to settle, one was brought to him who owed ten thousand talents.

cmp.note: 「他连得」是当时最大的钱数单位，一个他连得约合六千个银币，也就是一个工人将近二十年的工钱；「一万」又是希腊话里最大的数词。和合本折成「一千万银子」。
cmp.en: The talent was the largest unit of money, about six thousand denarii, close to twenty years of a laborer’s wages; and "ten thousand" is the largest number word in Greek. The Union Version converts it to 一千万银子 (yìqiān wàn yínzi, "ten million in silver").

verses.en: And since he did not have the means to repay, the master commanded him to be sold, with his wife and children and all that he has, and repayment to be made.
So the slave, falling down, was bowing before him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you everything.’
And the master of that slave, moved with compassion, released him and forgave him the loan.
But that slave, going out, found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred denarii, and seizing him he was choking him, saying, ‘Pay back what you owe.’
So his fellow slave, falling down, was pleading with him, saying, ‘Have patience with me, and I will repay you.’
But he was not willing; instead he went and threw him into prison until he should repay what was owed.
So when his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were greatly grieved, and they went and reported to their master all that had happened.
Then his master, calling him to him, says to him, ‘Wicked slave! All that debt I forgave you, since you pleaded with me;
should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, as I also had mercy on you?’
And his master, being angered, handed him over to the torturers until he should repay all that was owed.
So also my heavenly Father will do to you, if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.”

chapters.title: Chapter 19 · Divorce, Children, the Rich Young Man
chapters.intro: Jesus leaves Galilee for the part of Judea across the Jordan. Pharisees ask whether a man may divorce his wife for any reason; he answers that what God has joined no one should separate. Children are brought to him and he lays his hands on them. A rich young man asks how to gain eternal life and goes away grieving when told to sell what he owns, and Jesus says how hard it is for the rich to enter the kingdom of the heavens.

verses.en: And it happened, when Jesus had finished these words, that he departed from Galilee and came into the regions of Judea beyond the Jordan.
And large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
And Pharisees came to him, testing him and saying, “Is it permitted for a man to divorce his wife for any cause?”
And answering he said, “Have you not read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female
and said, ‘For this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh’?

cmp.note: 这两节引的是旧约《创世记》1:27 和 2:24。原文「你们没有念过吗」在上一节开头，和合本把它挪到了这一节末尾（「这经你们没有念过么」）。
cmp.en: These two verses quote Genesis 1:27 and 2:24. In the Greek, "Have you not read" stands at the start of the previous verse; the Union Version moves it to the end of this one as 这经你们没有念过么 (zhè jīng nǐmen méiyǒu niànguo me, "have you not read this scripture?").

verses.en: So they are no longer two but one flesh. What therefore God has joined together, let no man separate.”
They say to him, “Why then did Moses command to give a certificate of divorce and to send her away?”

cmp.note: 「休书」的规定出自旧约《申命记》24:1。
cmp.en: The rule about a "certificate of divorce" comes from Deuteronomy 24:1.

verses.en: He says to them, “Moses, because of your hardness of heart, permitted you to divorce your wives, but from the beginning it has not been so.
And I say to you, whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, and marries another commits adultery; and he who marries a divorced woman commits adultery.”
The disciples say to him, “If such is the case of a man with his wife, it is better not to marry.”
But he said to them, “Not all can accept this word, but those to whom it is given.

For there are eunuchs who were born so from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by men, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of the heavens. Let the one who is able to accept it accept it.”

cmp.note: 字面是「把自己做成阉人」。一般认为这第三种是比方的说法，指为了天国而不结婚的人，不是指真的动刀；经文自己没有解释。
cmp.en: Literally "made themselves eunuchs." This third kind is generally taken as a figure of speech for those who stay unmarried for the sake of the kingdom, not for a literal act; the text itself does not explain it.

verses.en: Then children were brought to him so that he might lay his hands on them and pray; but the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus said, “Let the children be, and do not hinder them from coming to me, for of such is the kingdom of the heavens.”
And having laid his hands on them, he went on from there.
And look, one came up to him and said, “Teacher, what good thing shall I do that I may have eternal life?”
And he said to him, “Why do you ask me about what is good? There is one who is good. But if you want to enter into life, keep the commandments.”
He says to him, “Which ones?” And Jesus said, “ ‘You shall not murder, You shall not commit adultery, You shall not steal, You shall not bear false witness,

cmp.note: 这几条出自旧约的「十诫」（《出埃及记》20:12–16）；下一节末尾的「爱邻人像爱自己」出自《利未记》19:18。
cmp.en: These come from the Ten Commandments (Exodus 20:12–16); "love your neighbor as yourself" at the end of the next verse is from Leviticus 19:18.

verses.en: Honor your father and mother,’ and, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’”
The young man says to him, “All these I have kept; what do I still lack?”
Jesus said to him, “If you want to be complete, go, sell your possessions and give to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven; and come, follow me.”
But when the young man heard this word, he went away grieving, for he had many possessions.
And Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I say to you, a rich man will enter the kingdom of the heavens with difficulty.
And again I say to you, it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.”

cmp.note: 这卷书平常说「天国」（字面是「诸天的国」），这里换成了「上帝的国」，两个说法指的是同一件事。
cmp.en: This Gospel usually says "the kingdom of the heavens"; here it has "the kingdom of God." The two expressions mean the same thing.

verses.en: And when the disciples heard, they were greatly astonished, saying, “Who then can be saved?”
And looking at them, Jesus said to them, “With men this is impossible, but with God all things are possible.”
Then Peter answered and said to him, “Look, we have left everything and followed you; what then will there be for us?”

And Jesus said to them, “Truly I say to you that you who have followed me, in the renewal, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, you also will sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.

cmp.note: 字面是「在重新出生的时候」，指世界被更新的那个时候。和合本译「复兴的时候」，白话写「万物更新的时候」。
cmp.en: Literally "in the rebirth," the time when the world is made new. The Union Version has 复兴的时候 (fùxīng de shíhou, "the time of revival"); the plain Chinese writes "when all things are renewed."

verses.en: And everyone who has left houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or fields for my name’s sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit eternal life.

cmp.note: 本站的底本在这串名单里有「妻子」，和合本没有；各种抄本在这里有出入。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows has "or wife" in this list; the Union Version does not. The manuscripts differ here.

verses.en: But many who are first will be last, and the last first.”

chapters.title: Chapter 20 · The Workers in the Vineyard; Who Would Be Great
chapters.intro: Jesus tells a parable: a landowner hires workers at several hours of the day and pays them all the same wage, and those hired first complain. On the way up to Jerusalem he tells the twelve for the third time that he will be put to death and raised on the third day. The mother of Zebedee’s sons asks for the highest places for them, and Jesus answers that whoever wants to be great must be a servant. Leaving Jericho, he heals two blind men.

verses.en: “For the kingdom of the heavens is like a man, a householder, who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
And having agreed with the workers for a denarius a day, he sent them into his vineyard.
And going out about the third hour, he saw others standing idle in the marketplace;

cmp.note: 原文照当时的算法，从日出数起：「第三时」「第六时」「第九时」「第十一时」。白话换成今天的钟点（上午九点、中午、下午三点、下午五点），英文照原文；和合本用的是中国旧时的「巳初、午正、申初、酉初」。
cmp.en: The Greek counts the hours from sunrise: the third, sixth, ninth and eleventh hour. The plain Chinese converts them to clock times (about 9 a.m., noon, 3 p.m. and 5 p.m.); the English keeps the original; the Union Version uses the old Chinese double-hours, such as 巳初 (sì chū, "start of the si hour").

verses.en: and to those he said, ‘You also go into the vineyard, and whatever is right I will give you.’
And they went. Going out again about the sixth and the ninth hour, he did likewise.
And about the eleventh, going out, he found others standing, and he says to them, ‘Why have you been standing here idle the whole day?’
They say to him, ‘Because no one hired us.’ He says to them, ‘You also go into the vineyard.’
And when evening came, the lord of the vineyard says to his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them the wage, beginning from the last up to the first.’
And those hired about the eleventh hour came and received a denarius each.
And when the first came, they supposed that they would receive more; and they also received a denarius each.
And having received it, they grumbled against the householder,
saying, ‘These last worked one hour, and you have made them equal to us who have borne the burden of the day and the scorching heat.’
But he answered one of them and said, ‘Friend, I am doing you no wrong; did you not agree with me for a denarius?
Take what is yours and go; I want to give to this last one the same as to you.
Is it not permitted for me to do what I want with what is mine? Or is your eye evil because I am good?’

cmp.note: 字面是「你的眼睛是坏的」，当时的说法，指嫉妒、小气。和合本译「红了眼」，白话写「眼红」。
cmp.en: Literally "your eye is evil," an idiom of the time for envy or stinginess. The Union Version has 红了眼 (hóng le yǎn, "your eyes went red," that is, jealous).

verses.en: So the last will be first, and the first last.”
And as Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the way he said to them,
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and scribes, and they will condemn him to death,
and they will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock and to scourge and to crucify, and on the third day he will be raised.”
Then the mother of the sons of Zebedee came to him with her sons, bowing down and asking something of him.
And he said to her, “What do you want?” She says to him, “Say that these two sons of mine may sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom.”
But Jesus answered and said, “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They say to him, “We are able.”
He says to them, “My cup you will drink, but to sit at my right and at my left is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
And when the ten heard, they were indignant about the two brothers.
But Jesus called them to him and said, “You know that the rulers of the Gentiles lord it over them, and the great ones exercise authority over them.
It will not be so among you; but whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant,
and whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave;
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served but to serve, and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
And as they were going out from Jericho, a large crowd followed him.
And look, two blind men sitting by the road, hearing that Jesus is passing by, cried out, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
And the crowd rebuked them so that they would be silent; but they cried out all the more, saying, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
And Jesus stood still and called them and said, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They say to him, “Lord, that our eyes may be opened.”
And moved with compassion, Jesus touched their eyes, and immediately they regained their sight and followed him.

chapters.title: Chapter 21 · Entering Jerusalem; Clearing the Temple
chapters.intro: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey while the crowds spread cloaks and branches on the road. He drives the traders out of the temple, and the next morning a fig tree with no fruit withers at his word. The chief priests and elders demand to know by what authority he acts; he asks them in return where John’s baptism came from, then tells the parables of the two sons and of the vineyard tenants, and they understand that he is speaking about them.

verses.en: And when they drew near to Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, to the Mount of Olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
saying to them, “Go into the village opposite you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied and a colt with her; untie them and bring them to me.
And if anyone says anything to you, you shall say, ‘The Lord has need of them,’ and immediately he will send them.”
Now this happened so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled, saying,
“Say to the daughter of Zion, ‘Look, your king is coming to you, gentle and mounted on a donkey, and on a colt, the foal of a beast of burden.’”

cmp.note: 这段话引自旧约《撒迦利亚书》9:9，开头一句出自《以赛亚书》62:11。「锡安的女儿」是对耶路撒冷这座城和城里人的称呼，和合本译「锡安的居民」。
cmp.en: The words are quoted from Zechariah 9:9, with the opening phrase from Isaiah 62:11. "Daughter of Zion" is a way of addressing the city of Jerusalem and its people; the Union Version renders it 锡安的居民 (Xī’ān de jūmín, "the inhabitants of Zion").

verses.en: And the disciples went and did just as Jesus directed them;
they brought the donkey and the colt and put their cloaks on them, and he sat on them.
And most of the crowd spread their own cloaks on the road, and others were cutting branches from the trees and spreading them on the road.
And the crowds going before him and those following were crying out, saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”

cmp.note: 「和散那」和「奉主的名来的那一位，是应当称颂的」出自旧约《诗篇》118:25–26，是犹太人过节时唱的句子。
cmp.en: "Hosanna" and "Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord" come from Psalm 118:25–26, lines sung at the Jewish festivals.

verses.en: And when he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was shaken, saying, “Who is this?”
And the crowds were saying, “This is the prophet Jesus, the one from Nazareth of Galilee.”
And Jesus entered the temple and drove out all who were selling and buying in the temple, and he overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling the doves,
and he says to them, “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you are making it a den of robbers.”

cmp.note: 前半句引自旧约《以赛亚书》56:7，「强盗窝」出自《耶利米书》7:11。
cmp.en: The first half is quoted from Isaiah 56:7; "den of robbers" is from Jeremiah 7:11.

verses.en: And blind and lame people came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
But when the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders that he did, and the children crying out in the temple and saying, “Hosanna to the Son of David,” they were indignant,
and they said to him, “Do you hear what these are saying?” And Jesus says to them, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of infants and nursing babies you have prepared praise’?”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》8:2，照的是当时通行的希腊文译本的字句。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 8:2, in the wording of the Greek translation in common use at the time.

verses.en: And leaving them, he went out of the city to Bethany and spent the night there.
Now in the morning, as he was returning to the city, he was hungry.
And seeing a single fig tree by the road, he went to it and found nothing on it except leaves only, and he says to it, “May no fruit ever come from you again.” And the fig tree withered at once.
And when the disciples saw it, they marveled, saying, “How did the fig tree wither at once?”

And Jesus answered and said to them, “Truly I say to you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Be lifted up and thrown into the sea,’ it will happen.
And all things, whatever you ask in prayer, believing, you will receive.”

And when he came into the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, saying, “By what authority are you doing these things? And who gave you this authority?”
And Jesus answered and said to them, “I also will ask you one thing, which if you tell me, I also will tell you by what authority I do these things.
The baptism of John, where was it from? From heaven or from men?” And they were reasoning among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Why then did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From men,’ we fear the crowd, for all hold John as a prophet.”
And they answered Jesus and said, “We do not know.” He also said to them, “Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
But what do you think? A man had two children. He came to the first and said, ‘Child, go work today in the vineyard.’
And he answered and said, ‘I will not’; but afterward he changed his mind and went.
And he came to the second and said the same. And he answered and said, ‘I will, sir’; and he did not go.

cmp.note: 字面只有「我，主人」两个词，意思是「我去，父亲大人」。这个比喻里两个儿子谁先谁后、谁去谁没去，各种抄本的次序不一样；本站的底本与和合本在这里一致。
cmp.en: Literally just "I, sir," meaning "I will go, sir." The manuscripts differ over the order of the two sons and which of them went; the edition this site follows agrees here with the Union Version.

verses.en: Which of the two did the will of the father?” They say, “The first.” Jesus says to them, “Truly I say to you that the tax collectors and the prostitutes are going ahead of you into the kingdom of God.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him; but the tax collectors and the prostitutes believed him; and you, seeing it, did not even change your minds afterward so as to believe him.
Hear another parable. There was a man, a householder, who planted a vineyard and put a fence around it and dug a winepress in it and built a tower, and he leased it to tenants and went on a journey.

cmp.note: 开辟葡萄园、围篱笆、挖榨酒池、盖楼，这几句是照着旧约《以赛亚书》5:1–2 说的，那里的葡萄园比的是以色列。
cmp.en: Planting the vineyard, fencing it, digging a winepress and building a tower echo Isaiah 5:1–2, where the vineyard stands for Israel.

verses.en: And when the season of the fruits drew near, he sent his slaves to the tenants to receive his fruits.
And the tenants took his slaves and beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
Again he sent other slaves, more than the first, and they did the same to them.
And afterward he sent his son to them, saying, ‘They will respect my son.’
But the tenants, seeing the son, said among themselves, ‘This is the heir; come, let us kill him and have his inheritance.’
And they took him and threw him out of the vineyard and killed him.
When therefore the lord of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those tenants?”
They say to him, “He will bring those wretches to a wretched end, and he will lease the vineyard to other tenants, who will give him the fruits in their seasons.”
Jesus says to them, “Have you never read in the scriptures, ‘The stone that the builders rejected, this has become the head of the corner; this came from the Lord, and it is marvelous in our eyes’?

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》118:22–23。「房角的头」指房角上最要紧的那块石头。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 118:22–23. "Head of the corner" means the most important stone at the corner of a building.

verses.en: Therefore I say to you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation producing its fruits.
And the one who falls on this stone will be broken to pieces; and on whomever it falls, it will crush him.”

cmp.note: 有少数抄本没有这一节；本站的底本与和合本都有。
cmp.en: A few manuscripts lack this verse; both the edition this site follows and the Union Version include it.

verses.en: And when the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they knew that he was speaking about them.
And though they were seeking to seize him, they feared the crowds, since they held him to be a prophet.

chapters.title: Chapter 22 · The Wedding Feast; Taxes, Resurrection, the Greatest Commandment
chapters.intro: Jesus tells a parable: a king gives a wedding feast for his son, the invited guests refuse to come, and people found on the roads are brought in instead. Then come a series of test questions: the Pharisees ask whether taxes should be paid to Caesar, the Sadducees ask whose wife a woman will be in the resurrection, and a lawyer asks which commandment is greatest. Finally Jesus asks whose son the Christ is, and no one can answer.

verses.en: And Jesus answered and spoke to them again in parables, saying,
“The kingdom of the heavens has become like a man, a king, who gave a wedding feast for his son.
And he sent his slaves to call those who had been invited to the wedding feast, and they did not want to come.

Again he sent other slaves, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited: Look, I have prepared my dinner; my oxen and the fattened cattle have been slaughtered, and everything is ready; come to the wedding feast.’
But they paid no attention and went off, one to his own field, another to his business;
and the rest seized his slaves, mistreated them, and killed them.
And the king was angered, and sending his troops he destroyed those murderers and burned their city.
Then he says to his slaves, ‘The wedding feast is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.
Go therefore to the outlets of the roads, and as many as you find, invite to the wedding feast.’
And those slaves went out into the roads and gathered all whom they found, both bad and good; and the wedding hall was filled with guests.
But when the king came in to look at the guests, he saw there a man not dressed in a wedding garment;
and he says to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here not having a wedding garment?’ And he was speechless.
Then the king said to the attendants, ‘Bind his feet and hands and throw him out into the outer darkness; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.’
For many are called, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and took counsel how they might trap him in a word.

And they send their disciples to him, with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God in truth, and you do not care about anyone, for you do not look at the face of men.
Tell us therefore, what do you think? Is it permitted to give the poll tax to Caesar or not?”
But Jesus, knowing their wickedness, said, “Why are you testing me, hypocrites?
Show me the coin for the tax.” And they brought him a denarius.
And he says to them, “Whose is this image and inscription?”
They say to him, “Caesar’s.” Then he says to them, “Give back therefore to Caesar the things that are Caesar’s, and to God the things that are God’s.”
And when they heard, they marveled, and leaving him they went away.
On that day Sadducees came to him, saying that there is no resurrection, and they questioned him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If anyone dies having no children, his brother shall marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’

cmp.note: 这条规定出自旧约《申命记》25:5：哥哥死了没有儿子，弟弟要娶嫂子，生的头一个儿子算在哥哥名下。
cmp.en: The rule comes from Deuteronomy 25:5: if a man dies without a son, his brother is to marry the widow, and the first son born counts as the dead man’s.

verses.en: Now there were seven brothers among us; and the first married and died, and having no offspring he left his wife to his brother.
Likewise also the second and the third, down to the seventh.
And last of all the woman died.
In the resurrection, therefore, whose wife of the seven will she be? For they all had her.”
But Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken, knowing neither the scriptures nor the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage, but are like angels of God in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, saying,
‘I am the God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead but of the living.”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《出埃及记》3:6，是上帝在烧着的荆棘里对摩西说的话。
cmp.en: Quoted from Exodus 3:6, words God speaks to Moses from the burning bush.

verses.en: And when the crowds heard, they were astonished at his teaching.
But the Pharisees, hearing that he had silenced the Sadducees, gathered together.
And one of them, a lawyer, questioned him, testing him:
“Teacher, which commandment is great in the law?”
And he said to him, “ ‘You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind.’

cmp.note: 引自旧约《申命记》6:5；第 39 节的「爱邻人像爱自己」引自《利未记》19:18。和合本把三个「全部的」译成「尽心、尽性、尽意」。
cmp.en: Quoted from Deuteronomy 6:5; "love your neighbor as yourself" in verse 39 is from Leviticus 19:18. The Union Version renders the three phrases as 尽心、尽性、尽意 (jìn xīn, jìn xìng, jìn yì, "with all the heart, all the nature, all the intent").

verses.en: This is the great and first commandment.
And a second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets.”

cmp.note: 原文的动词是「挂」：全部经书像挂在这两个钉子上。「律法和先知」是当时对整部犹太经书的叫法。和合本译成「是律法和先知一切道理的总纲」。
cmp.en: The Greek verb is "hang": the whole of scripture hangs on these two as on pegs. "The law and the prophets" was the usual name for the Jewish scriptures as a whole. The Union Version has 总纲 (zǒnggāng, "the summary").

verses.en: Now while the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They say to him, “David’s.”
He says to them, “How then does David in the Spirit call him Lord, saying,
‘The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet’?

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》110:1，传统上认为这首诗是大卫写的。头一个「主」指上帝，第二个「我的主」指大卫所说的那一位。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 110:1, a psalm traditionally ascribed to David. The first "Lord" is God; "my Lord" is the one David is speaking of.

verses.en: If therefore David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
And no one was able to answer him a word, nor did anyone dare from that day to question him any longer.

chapters.title: Chapter 23 · Woes against the Scribes and Pharisees
chapters.intro: Jesus tells the crowds and his disciples to do what the scribes and Pharisees teach but not to copy what they do, since they say and do not do, and act in order to be seen. He then says "Woe to you" seven times, charging them with pretense, with caring only for the outside, and with killing the prophets. He ends with a lament over Jerusalem. From verse 2 to the end it is all Jesus speaking.

verses.en: Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and to his disciples,
saying, “The scribes and the Pharisees have sat down on the seat of Moses.
Therefore all that they tell you, do and keep; but do not do according to their works, for they say and do not do.
And they tie up heavy burdens and lay them on people’s shoulders, but they themselves are not willing to move them with their finger.
And they do all their works to be seen by people; for they make their phylacteries broad and their tassels long,

cmp.note: 经文匣是装着几段经文的小皮盒，犹太男子祷告时绑在额头和左臂上（照《申命记》6:8 的话）；衣角的穗子是照《民数记》15:38 的规定缝的，提醒人记住诫命。
cmp.en: Phylacteries are small leather boxes holding passages of scripture, bound on the forehead and left arm by Jewish men at prayer (following Deuteronomy 6:8); the tassels on the corners of the garment follow the rule in Numbers 15:38 and are a reminder of the commandments.

verses.en: and they love the place of honor at dinners and the chief seats in the synagogues
and the greetings in the marketplaces and to be called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
But you, do not be called ‘Rabbi,’ for one is your teacher, and you are all brothers.
And call no one your father on the earth, for one is your Father, the heavenly one.
Neither be called instructors, for your instructor is one, the Christ.
And the greatest among you will be your servant.
And whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you shut the kingdom of the heavens in front of people; for you do not enter, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in.

cmp.note: 这个词本来指戏台上的演员，引申为装出一副样子给人看的人。和合本译「假冒为善」，白话写「装模作样」。
cmp.en: The word originally meant a stage actor, and so someone who puts on a show for others. The Union Version has 假冒为善 (jiǎmào wéi shàn, "pretending to be good"); the plain Chinese writes "putting on an act."

verses.en: (This verse is not in the Greek edition this site follows.)

cmp.note: 较晚的抄本在这里（有的在第 13 节前面）还有一句「你们有祸了」，说文士和法利赛人吞没寡妇的家产，又装样子做很长的祷告，所以要受更重的审判。最早的几份抄本没有这一句，一般认为是抄写的人从《马可福音》12:40、《路加福音》20:47 补进来的，所以底本不收。节号照旧留着，后面各节的编号才不会变。
cmp.en: Later manuscripts have here (some before verse 13) one more "Woe to you," saying that the scribes and Pharisees devour widows’ houses and make long prayers for show, and so will receive a heavier judgment. The earliest manuscripts lack it, and it is generally thought that copyists brought it in from Mark 12:40 and Luke 20:47, so the edition leaves it out. The verse number is kept so that the verses after it keep their numbering.

verses.en: Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you travel over sea and dry land to make one convert, and when he becomes one, you make him a son of Gehenna twice as much as yourselves.

cmp.note: 「某某之子」是希伯来话的说法，意思是「属于某某的人」；「地狱之子」就是该下地狱的人。原文的「地狱」是「欣嫩谷」这个地名，英文照音写。
cmp.en: "Son of" something is a Hebrew way of saying "one who belongs to" it; a "son of Gehenna" is someone bound for it. The Greek word is the place name Gehenna, the Valley of Hinnom, which the English keeps; both Chinese versions write 地狱 (dìyù, "hell").

verses.en: Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the sanctuary, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gold of the sanctuary is bound.’
Fools and blind! For which is greater, the gold or the sanctuary that made the gold holy?
And, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it is nothing; but whoever swears by the gift that is on it is bound.’
Blind men! For which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy?
Therefore the one who swears by the altar swears by it and by everything on it;
and the one who swears by the sanctuary swears by it and by the one who dwells in it;
and the one who swears by heaven swears by the throne of God and by the one who sits on it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you tithe mint and dill and cumin, and have left aside the weightier matters of the law: justice and mercy and faithfulness. These you ought to have done, without leaving the others aside.
Blind guides, who strain out the gnat but swallow the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but inside they are full of robbery and self-indulgence.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish, so that the outside of it may also become clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you are like whitewashed tombs, which outwardly appear beautiful but inside are full of dead men’s bones and all uncleanness.
So you also outwardly appear righteous to people, but inside you are full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites, because you build the tombs of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
and you say, ‘If we had been in the days of our fathers, we would not have been partners with them in the blood of the prophets.’
So you testify against yourselves that you are sons of those who murdered the prophets.
You then, fill up the measure of your fathers.
Serpents, offspring of vipers, how are you to escape the judgment of Gehenna?
Therefore, look, I am sending to you prophets and wise men and scribes; some of them you will kill and crucify, and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues and pursue from city to city,

so that upon you may come all the righteous blood poured out on the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Barachiah, whom you murdered between the sanctuary and the altar.

cmp.note: 亚伯是旧约里第一个被杀的人（《创世记》第 4 章）。在圣殿院子里被杀的撒迦利亚见《历代志下》24:20–22，那里说他父亲叫耶何耶大；这卷书排在希伯来经书的最后，所以「从亚伯到撒迦利亚」一般理解为「从头到尾」。
cmp.en: Abel is the first person killed in the Old Testament (Genesis 4). The Zechariah killed in the temple court is found in 2 Chronicles 24:20–22, where his father is called Jehoiada; that book stands last in the Hebrew scriptures, so "from Abel to Zechariah" is generally understood as "from beginning to end."

verses.en: Truly I say to you, all these things will come upon this generation.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, who kills the prophets and stones those sent to her—how often I wanted to gather your children, the way a hen gathers her chicks under her wings, and you were not willing!
Look, your house is left to you desolate.
For I say to you, you will certainly not see me from now on until you say, ‘Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord.’”

cmp.note: 引自旧约《诗篇》118:26，和第 21 章人群迎接耶稣进城时喊的是同一句。
cmp.en: Quoted from Psalm 118:26, the same line the crowds shouted when Jesus entered the city in chapter 21.

chapters.title: Chapter 24 · The Temple’s Fall Foretold; the Coming of the Son of Man
chapters.intro: Jesus says the temple will be torn down until not one stone is left on another. On the Mount of Olives the disciples ask him privately when this will happen and what will be the sign of his coming and of the end of the age. He speaks of wars, persecution, a great tribulation and impostors, says the Son of Man will come on the clouds, and that no one knows the day, so they must keep awake. From verse 4 to the end of chapter 25 Jesus is speaking without a break.

verses.en: And Jesus, having gone out from the temple, was going on his way, and his disciples came to him to point out to him the buildings of the temple.
But he answered and said to them, “Do you not see all these things? Truly I say to you, there will not be left here a stone upon a stone that will not be thrown down.”
And as he was sitting on the Mount of Olives, the disciples came to him privately, saying, “Tell us, when will these things be, and what will be the sign of your coming and of the end of the age?”

cmp.note: 字面是「来到」「在场」，当时也用来说君王驾临一座城。和合本译「降临」。四卷福音书里只有《马太福音》用这个词，都在这一章（第 3、27、37、39 节）。
cmp.en: Literally "arrival" or "presence," a word also used at the time for a ruler’s visit to a city. The Union Version has 降临 (jiànglín, "descend"). Among the four Gospels only Matthew uses the word, all in this chapter (verses 3, 27, 37, 39).

verses.en: And Jesus answered and said to them, “See that no one leads you astray.
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.
And you are going to hear of wars and rumors of wars; see that you are not alarmed; for it must happen, but the end is not yet.
For nation will rise against nation and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places;
but all these are the beginning of birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to tribulation and will kill you, and you will be hated by all the nations because of my name.
And then many will stumble and will hand one another over and hate one another;
and many false prophets will arise and lead many astray;
and because lawlessness is multiplied, the love of the many will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end, this one will be saved.
And this good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed in the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all the nations, and then the end will come.
So when you see the abomination of desolation, spoken of through Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—

cmp.note: 这个说法出自旧约《但以理书》（9:27、11:31、12:11），一般认为那里指的是公元前二世纪外族君王在耶路撒冷圣殿里设异教祭坛的事。经文没有说明这里指什么，只插了一句「读的人要明白」；这一句是原文就有的，所以本站没有放进圆括号。
cmp.en: The phrase comes from the Old Testament book of Daniel (9:27; 11:31; 12:11), where it is generally taken to refer to a foreign king setting up a pagan altar in the Jerusalem temple in the second century BCE. The text does not say what it refers to here; it only inserts "let the reader understand," which is part of the original and so is not put in parentheses in the Chinese.

verses.en: then let those in Judea flee to the mountains,
let the one on the housetop not come down to take the things out of his house,
and let the one in the field not turn back to take his cloak.
But woe to those who are pregnant and to those who are nursing in those days!
And pray that your flight may not happen in winter or on a Sabbath;
for then there will be great tribulation, such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, and never will be.
And if those days had not been cut short, no flesh would be saved; but for the sake of the chosen those days will be cut short.
Then if anyone says to you, ‘Look, here is the Christ!’ or ‘Here!’ do not believe it.
For false christs and false prophets will arise and will give great signs and wonders, so as to lead astray, if possible, even the chosen.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
So if they say to you, ‘Look, he is in the wilderness,’ do not go out; ‘Look, he is in the inner rooms,’ do not believe it.
For as the lightning comes out from the east and shines as far as the west, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Wherever the corpse is, there the eagles will be gathered.

cmp.note: 这个词可以指鹰，也可以指吃腐肉的秃鹫。这一句像是一句俗语，经文没有解释它在这里的意思。
cmp.en: The word can mean eagles or carrion-eating vultures. The line sounds like a proverb, and the text does not explain what it means here.

verses.en: And immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light, and the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
And then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in heaven, and then all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.

cmp.w: erchomenon epi tōn nephelōn tou ouranou
cmp.note: 「驾着天上的云来」引的是旧约《但以理书》7:13：那里说有一位「像人子的」驾着天上的云来，从上帝那里得到权柄。
cmp.en: "Coming on the clouds of heaven" echoes Daniel 7:13 in the Old Testament, where "one like a son of man" comes with the clouds of heaven and receives authority from God.

verses.en: And he will send out his angels with a great trumpet, and they will gather his chosen from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
From the fig tree learn the parable: when its branch has already become tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near.
So also you, when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors.

cmp.note: 原文只有「近了」，没有主语，可以读成「他近了」，也可以读成「那事近了」。白话和英文取「他」；和合本直接补成「人子近了」。
cmp.en: The Greek has only "is near," with no subject; it can be read as "he is near" or "it is near." Both translations here take "he"; the Union Version supplies 人子 (Rénzǐ, "the Son of Man").

verses.en: Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But concerning that day and hour no one knows, neither the angels of the heavens nor the Son, but the Father alone.

cmp.note: 「子也不知道」这几个字，不少抄本在《马太福音》这里没有（《马可福音》13:32 各抄本都有）。本站的底本有，和合本也有。
cmp.en: Many manuscripts of Matthew lack the words "nor the Son" here (all manuscripts have them at Mark 13:32). The edition this site follows includes them, and so does the Union Version.

verses.en: For as the days of Noah were, so will be the coming of the Son of Man.
For as in those days before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day Noah entered the ark,
and they did not know until the flood came and swept them all away, so also will be the coming of the Son of Man.
Then two men will be in the field: one is taken and one is left;
two women grinding at the mill: one is taken and one is left.
So keep awake, for you do not know on what day your Lord is coming.
But know this: if the master of the house had known in what watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have kept awake and would not have let his house be dug through.
Therefore you also be ready, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
Who then is the faithful and wise slave, whom the master has set over his household, to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master, when he comes, will find doing so.
Truly I say to you, he will set him over all his possessions.
But if that bad slave says in his heart, ‘My master is delayed,’
and begins to beat his fellow slaves, and eats and drinks with the drunkards,
the master of that slave will come on a day when he does not expect and at an hour he does not know,
and will cut him in two and put his portion with the hypocrites; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.

cmp.note: 原文字面是「砍成两段」，和合本译成「重重的处治他」。「哀哭，咬牙切齿」这句话在这卷书里出现六次（8:12、13:42、13:50、22:13、24:51、25:30）。
cmp.en: The Greek is literally "will cut in two"; the Union Version softens it to 重重的处治他 (zhòngzhòng de chǔzhì tā, "punish him severely"). The line about weeping and gnashing of teeth occurs six times in this book (8:12; 13:42; 13:50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30).

chapters.title: Chapter 25 · The Ten Virgins, the Talents, the Sheep and the Goats
chapters.intro: Jesus goes straight on from the previous chapter without a pause, which is why this chapter opens with no quotation mark. He tells three things in a row: ten young women wait for a bridegroom, and five have not brought enough oil; a master going abroad entrusts money to three slaves and settles accounts on his return; and finally the Son of Man sits on his throne and, as a shepherd separates sheep from goats, divides all people into two groups by how they treated the least.

verses.en: Then the kingdom of the heavens will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
And five of them were foolish and five were wise.
For the foolish, when they took their lamps, took no oil with them;
but the wise took oil in flasks along with their lamps.
And as the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and were sleeping.
But at midnight there was a cry: ‘Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him.’
Then all those virgins got up and trimmed their lamps.
And the foolish said to the wise, ‘Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.’
But the wise answered, saying, ‘There may not be enough for us and for you; go rather to those who sell, and buy for yourselves.’
And while they were going away to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut.
And later the other virgins also come, saying, ‘Lord, lord, open to us.’
But he answered and said, ‘Truly I say to you, I do not know you.’
So keep awake, for you do not know the day or the hour.
For it is like a man going away on a journey, who called his own slaves and handed over to them his possessions,
and to one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, to each according to his own ability, and he went away. Immediately

cmp.note: 他连得本来是重量单位，也用来计钱。一他连得银子大约合六千个银币，一个银币约是一天的工钱，所以一他连得是一个工人十几二十年的工钱。和合本换算成「五千」「二千」「一千」（两银子）。底本把「立刻」放在这一节末尾，属于下一节的句子，英文照底本的断法。
cmp.en: A talent was a unit of weight, also used to count money. A talent of silver was about six thousand denarii, a denarius being roughly a day’s wage, so one talent was what a laborer earned in fifteen or twenty years. The Union Version converts the sums to 五千, 二千, 一千 (wǔqiān, èrqiān, yīqiān, "five thousand, two thousand, one thousand" of silver). The edition puts "Immediately" at the end of this verse although it belongs to the next sentence; the English keeps that division.

verses.en: the one who had received the five talents went and worked with them and gained five more;
likewise the one with the two gained two more;
but the one who had received the one went off and dug in the ground and hid his master’s silver.
And after a long time the master of those slaves comes and settles accounts with them.
And the one who had received the five talents came forward and brought five more talents, saying, ‘Master, you handed over to me five talents; see, I have gained five more talents.’
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many; enter into the joy of your master.’
And the one with the two talents also came forward and said, ‘Master, you handed over to me two talents; see, I have gained two more talents.’
His master said to him, ‘Well done, good and faithful slave; you were faithful over a few things, I will set you over many; enter into the joy of your master.’
And the one who had received the one talent also came forward and said, ‘Master, I knew you, that you are a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering from where you did not scatter;
and being afraid, I went off and hid your talent in the ground; see, you have what is yours.’
But his master answered and said to him, ‘Wicked and lazy slave, you knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather from where I did not scatter?
Then you ought to have put my silver with the bankers, and on my coming I would have received what is mine with interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents;
for to everyone who has, more will be given, and he will have abundance; but from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
And throw the worthless slave into the outer darkness; there will be the weeping and the gnashing of teeth.’
But when the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory;
and all the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as the shepherd separates the sheep from the goats,
and he will set the sheep on his right and the goats on the left.
Then the king will say to those on his right, ‘Come, you blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry and you gave me to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you took me in,
naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me.’
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink?
And when did we see you a stranger and take you in, or naked and clothe you?
And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?’
And the king will answer and say to them, ‘Truly I say to you, inasmuch as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.’
Then he will say also to those on the left, ‘Go away from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry and you did not give me to eat, I was thirsty and you did not give me drink,
I was a stranger and you did not take me in, naked and you did not clothe me, sick and in prison and you did not visit me.’
Then they also will answer, saying, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison, and did not serve you?’
Then he will answer them, saying, ‘Truly I say to you, inasmuch as you did not do it to one of the least of these, you did not do it to me either.’
And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.”

chapters.title: Chapter 26 · The Last Supper, the Arrest, the Trial
chapters.intro: Two days before the Passover the chief priests and elders plot to get rid of Jesus, and his disciple Judas agrees to hand him over for thirty pieces of silver. A woman pours very costly ointment on his head. Jesus eats the Passover meal with the twelve and speaks of the bread and the cup as his body and blood. That night he prays in Gethsemane, is arrested, is tried before the high priest and judged deserving of death, while Peter three times denies knowing him.

verses.en: And it happened, when Jesus had finished all these words, that he said to his disciples,
“You know that after two days the Passover comes, and the Son of Man is handed over to be crucified.”
Then the chief priests and the elders of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas,
and they plotted together to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him;
but they said, “Not during the festival, lest there be an uproar among the people.”
Now when Jesus was in Bethany in the house of Simon the leper,
a woman came to him having an alabaster jar of very costly ointment, and she poured it over his head as he was reclining at table.
But when the disciples saw it they were indignant, saying, “Why this waste?
For this could have been sold for much and given to the poor.”
But Jesus, knowing it, said to them, “Why do you cause trouble for the woman? For she has done a good work on me.
For you always have the poor with you, but me you do not always have.
For in pouring this ointment on my body, she did it to prepare me for burial.
Truly I say to you, wherever this good news is proclaimed in the whole world, what she has done will also be told in memory of her.”
Then one of the twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and said, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?” And they weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver.

cmp.note: 「称了三十块银子」的说法和旧约《撒迦利亚书》11:12 一样；第 27 章第 9 节会再提到这笔钱。和合本写「给了他三十块钱」。
cmp.en: The wording "weighed out thirty pieces of silver" matches Zechariah 11:12 in the Old Testament; the money comes up again at 27:9. The Union Version writes 给了他三十块钱 (gěi le tā sānshí kuài qián, "gave him thirty pieces of money").

verses.en: And from then on he was seeking an opportunity to hand him over.
Now on the first day of the Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus, saying, “Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?”
And he said, “Go into the city to a certain man and say to him, ‘The Teacher says: My time is near; at your house I am keeping the Passover with my disciples.’”
And the disciples did as Jesus had directed them, and they prepared the Passover.
And when evening came, he was reclining at table with the twelve disciples;
and as they were eating he said, “Truly I say to you, one of you will hand me over.”

cmp.note: 原文是「交出去」，和合本在这几章都译成「卖」。这卷书里同一个动词也用来说施洗的约翰被抓（4:12）、耶稣被交给外族人（20:19），所以白话统一写「交出去」。
cmp.en: The Greek is "hand over"; in these chapters the Union Version renders it 卖 (mài, "sell, betray"). The same verb is used in this book for the arrest of John the Baptist (4:12) and for Jesus being handed over to the Gentiles (20:19), so both translations keep "hand over" throughout.

verses.en: And being greatly grieved, they began to say to him, each one, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
But he answered and said, “The one who dipped his hand with me in the bowl, this one will hand me over.
The Son of Man goes as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man is handed over! It would be better for him if that man had not been born.”
And Judas, the one handing him over, answered and said, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He says to him, “You have said it.”

cmp.note: 字面是「你说了」。和合本译「你说的是」，当成直接的承认；原文的说法比较含蓄，没有直接说「是」。第 64 节耶稣回答大祭司、27:11 回答彼拉多，用的是同样的说法。
cmp.en: Literally "You said (it)." The Union Version has 你说的是 (nǐ shuō de shì, "what you say is so"), a plain yes; the Greek is more reserved and does not say "yes" outright. Jesus answers the high priest in verse 64, and Pilate at 27:11, in the same way.

verses.en: And as they were eating, Jesus took bread, and having blessed it he broke it, and giving it to the disciples he said, “Take, eat; this is my body.”
And taking a cup and having given thanks, he gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you,
for this is my blood of the covenant, which is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
But I say to you, from now on I will not drink of this fruit of the vine until that day when I drink it new with you in the kingdom of my Father.”
And having sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
