Then Jesus says to them, “You will all fall away because of me this night, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’

cmp.note: 单引号里的话引自旧约《撒迦利亚书》13:7。
cmp.en: The words in single quotation marks are from Zechariah 13:7 in the Old Testament.

verses.en: But after I am raised, I will go ahead of you into Galilee.”
But Peter answered and said to him, “If all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.”
Jesus said to him, “Truly I say to you that this very night, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.”
Peter says to him, “Even if I must die with you, I will not deny you.” And all the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus comes with them to a place called Gethsemane, and he says to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
And taking with him Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be grieved and troubled.
Then he says to them, “My soul is deeply grieved, to the point of death; remain here and keep awake with me.”
And going a little farther, he fell on his face, praying and saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass from me; yet not as I will, but as you will.”
And he comes to the disciples and finds them sleeping, and he says to Peter, “So, were you not strong enough to keep awake with me one hour?
Keep awake and pray, that you may not come into testing; the spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again, a second time, he went away and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass unless I drink it, let your will be done.”
And coming again he found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
And leaving them, he went away again and prayed a third time, saying the same words again.
Then he comes to the disciples and says to them, “Are you still sleeping and resting? Look, the hour has come near, and the Son of Man is handed over into the hands of sinners.

cmp.note: 这半句可以读成问句（「你们还在睡觉、还在休息吗？」），也可以读成一句吩咐（「你们接着睡、歇着吧」）。和合本取后一种；白话和英文取问句，和《马可福音》14:41 的译法一致。
cmp.en: This clause can be read as a question ("Are you still sleeping and resting?") or as a command ("Sleep on now and rest"). The Union Version takes it as a command; both translations here take it as a question, as at Mark 14:41.

verses.en: Rise, let us go; look, the one handing me over has come near.”
And while he was still speaking, look, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now the one handing him over had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is he; seize him.”
And immediately he went up to Jesus and said, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and he kissed him.
But Jesus said to him, “Friend, that for which you are here.” Then they came forward and laid hands on Jesus and seized him.

cmp.note: 原文只有半句话：「你到这里来要做的那件事」，没有说完。可以理解成「就做吧」（和合本和白话这样补），也有人读成问句「你来做什么？」。英文照原文留着半句。
cmp.en: The Greek is only half a sentence: "that for which you are here." It can be completed as "do it" (so the Union Version, and the Chinese here, in parentheses), and some read it as a question, "Why are you here?" The English leaves it unfinished as in the Greek.

verses.en: And look, one of those with Jesus stretched out his hand and drew his sword, and striking the slave of the high priest he cut off his ear.
Then Jesus says to him, “Put your sword back into its place; for all who take the sword will perish by the sword.
Or do you think that I cannot call on my Father, and he will at once send me more than twelve legions of angels?
How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that it must happen in this way?”
In that hour Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out as against a bandit, with swords and clubs, to capture me? Day after day I sat in the temple teaching, and you did not seize me.
But all this has happened so that the scriptures of the prophets might be fulfilled.” Then all the disciples left him and fled.
Now those who had seized Jesus led him away to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and the elders had gathered.
And Peter was following him from a distance as far as the courtyard of the high priest, and going inside he was sitting with the attendants to see the end.
Now the chief priests and the whole council were seeking false testimony against Jesus so that they might put him to death,
and they found none, though many false witnesses came forward. But later two came forward
and said, “This man said, ‘I am able to destroy the temple of God and to build it in three days.’”
And the high priest stood up and said to him, “Do you answer nothing? What is it that these men testify against you?”
But Jesus was silent. And the high priest said to him, “I put you under oath by the living God, that you tell us if you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus says to him, “You have said it. But I say to you, from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”

cmp.note: 原文是「从现在起」，和合本译成「后来」。这句话合用了旧约的两处：「坐在右边」出自《诗篇》110:1，「驾着天上的云来」出自《但以理书》7:13。
cmp.en: The Greek is "from now on"; the Union Version has 后来 (hòulái, "later"). The saying joins two Old Testament passages: "sitting at the right hand" from Psalm 110:1 and "coming on the clouds of heaven" from Daniel 7:13.

verses.en: Then the high priest tore his garments, saying, “He has blasphemed! What further need do we have of witnesses? See, now you have heard the blasphemy.
What do you think?” And they answered and said, “He deserves death.”
Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists, and some slapped him,
saying, “Prophesy to us, Christ: who is it that struck you?”
Now Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard, and a servant girl came up to him, saying, “You also were with Jesus the Galilean.”
But he denied it before them all, saying, “I do not know what you are saying.”
And when he went out to the gateway, another saw him and says to those there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazorean.”
And again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man.”
And after a little while those standing there came up and said to Peter, “Truly you also are one of them, for your speech gives you away.”
Then he began to curse and to swear, “I do not know the man.” And immediately a rooster crowed.
And Peter remembered the word of Jesus, who had said, “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” And he went outside and wept bitterly.

chapters.title: Chapter 27 · Before Pilate; the Crucifixion and Burial
chapters.intro: In the morning the chief priests and elders hand Jesus over to the Roman governor Pilate; Judas, filled with remorse, returns the silver and hangs himself. Pilate is inclined to release Jesus, but the crowd asks for Barabbas and for Jesus to be crucified. The soldiers mock him and crucify him at Golgotha. From noon darkness covers the land, and about three in the afternoon he dies. In the evening Joseph lays him in a new tomb, and the chief priests have it guarded.

verses.en: Now when morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to put him to death;
and having bound him they led him away and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, the one who handed him over, seeing that he was condemned, felt remorse and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
saying, “I have sinned, handing over innocent blood.” But they said, “What is that to us? See to it yourself.”
And throwing the pieces of silver into the temple, he departed, and going away he hanged himself.
But the chief priests, taking the pieces of silver, said, “It is not lawful to put them into the treasury, since it is the price of blood.”
And having taken counsel, they bought with them the Potter’s Field as a burial place for strangers.
Therefore that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

Then was fulfilled what was spoken through Jeremiah the prophet, saying, “And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one who was priced, on whom some of the sons of Israel had set a price,

cmp.note: 经文说这是先知耶利米的话。这段引文的字句最接近旧约《撒迦利亚书》11:12–13；陶匠和买田的事则见于《耶利米书》（第 19 章、第 32 章）。
cmp.en: The text attributes the saying to the prophet Jeremiah. Its wording is closest to Zechariah 11:12–13 in the Old Testament, while a potter and the buying of a field appear in Jeremiah (chapters 19 and 32).

verses.en: and they gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord directed me.”
Now Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor questioned him, saying, “Are you the King of the Jews?” And Jesus said, “You say so.”
And while he was being accused by the chief priests and elders, he answered nothing.
Then Pilate says to him, “Do you not hear how many things they testify against you?”
And he did not answer him, not even to a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
Now at the festival the governor was accustomed to release for the crowd one prisoner whom they wanted.
And they had then a notorious prisoner called Jesus Barabbas.

cmp.note: 本站的底本在这一节和下一节写的是「耶稣巴拉巴」，就是说这个囚犯也叫耶稣（当时很常见的名字）。多数抄本只有「巴拉巴」，和合本也是。
cmp.en: The edition this site follows reads "Jesus Barabbas" in this verse and the next: the prisoner too was named Jesus, a very common name at the time. Most manuscripts have only "Barabbas," and so does the Union Version.

verses.en: So when they had gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release for you: Jesus Barabbas, or Jesus who is called Christ?”
For he knew that it was out of envy that they had handed him over.
And while he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent to him, saying, “Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much today in a dream because of him.”
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowds to ask for Barabbas and to destroy Jesus.
And the governor answered and said to them, “Which of the two do you want me to release for you?” And they said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate says to them, “What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ?” They all say, “Let him be crucified!”
But he said, “Why, what evil has he done?” But they were crying out all the more, saying, “Let him be crucified!”

And Pilate, seeing that he was gaining nothing but rather that an uproar was starting, took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this man’s blood; see to it yourselves.”
And all the people answered and said, “His blood be on us and on our children.”
Then he released Barabbas for them, and having had Jesus flogged, he handed him over to be crucified.
Then the soldiers of the governor, taking Jesus into the praetorium, gathered the whole cohort around him.
And stripping him, they put a scarlet cloak around him,
and having woven a crown of thorns they put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand, and kneeling before him they mocked him, saying, “Hail, King of the Jews!”
And spitting on him, they took the reed and were striking him on the head.
And when they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak and put his own clothes on him, and led him away to crucify him.
And as they were going out, they found a man of Cyrene, Simon by name; this man they compelled to carry his cross.
And coming to a place called Golgotha, which means Place of a Skull,
they gave him wine to drink mixed with gall; and having tasted it, he would not drink.
And having crucified him, they divided his garments, casting lots,
and sitting down they were keeping watch over him there.
And they put above his head the charge against him, written: “This is Jesus, the King of the Jews.”
Then two bandits are crucified with him, one on the right and one on the left.
And those passing by were reviling him, shaking their heads
and saying, “You who destroy the temple and build it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross.”
Likewise also the chief priests, mocking with the scribes and elders, were saying,
“He saved others; himself he cannot save. He is the King of Israel; let him come down now from the cross, and we will believe in him.
He trusts in God; let him rescue him now, if he wants him; for he said, ‘I am God’s Son.’”

cmp.note: 这一句的说法和旧约《诗篇》22:8 很接近：那里是旁人嘲笑一个受苦的人，说他既然倚靠上帝，就让上帝来救他。
cmp.en: The wording is close to Psalm 22:8 in the Old Testament, where onlookers mock a sufferer: he relied on God, so let God rescue him.

verses.en: And the bandits who were crucified with him were reviling him in the same way.
Now from the sixth hour darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
And about the ninth hour Jesus cried out with a loud voice, saying, “Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?” that is, “My God, my God, why have you forsaken me?”

cmp.note: 经文先照原话的读音写下来，再翻成希腊文。这句话是旧约《诗篇》第 22 篇的第一句。《马可福音》15:34 写的是亚兰话的「以罗伊」；这里写「以利」，更接近希伯来话，后半句仍是亚兰话。「以利」和「以利亚」读音相近，所以下一节旁边的人以为他在叫以利亚。
cmp.en: The text first writes the words as they sounded and then translates them into Greek. They are the opening line of Psalm 22. Mark 15:34 has the Aramaic form "Eloi"; here it is "Eli," closer to Hebrew, while the rest of the sentence is still Aramaic. "Eli" sounds like "Elijah," which is why the bystanders in the next verse think he is calling Elijah.

verses.en: And some of those standing there, hearing it, were saying, “This man is calling Elijah.”
And immediately one of them ran and, taking a sponge and filling it with sour wine and putting it on a reed, was giving him a drink.
But the rest were saying, “Wait, let us see whether Elijah comes to save him.”
But Jesus, crying out again with a loud voice, gave up his spirit.
And look, the curtain of the temple was torn in two from top to bottom, and the earth shook, and the rocks were split,
and the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had fallen asleep were raised,
and coming out of the tombs after his rising they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
Now the centurion and those with him keeping watch over Jesus, seeing the earthquake and the things that happened, were greatly afraid, saying, “Truly this was God’s Son.”
And many women were there watching from a distance, who had followed Jesus from Galilee, serving him;
among whom were Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James and Joseph, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
Now when evening came, there came a rich man from Arimathea, Joseph by name, who had himself also become a disciple of Jesus;
this man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus. Then Pilate ordered it to be given.
And taking the body, Joseph wrapped it in a clean linen cloth
and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn in the rock; and having rolled a large stone against the door of the tomb, he went away.
And Mary Magdalene was there, and the other Mary, sitting opposite the tomb.
Now on the next day, which is the one after the Preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered before Pilate,
saying, “Sir, we remember that that deceiver said while he was still alive, ‘After three days I am raised.’

Therefore order the tomb to be made secure until the third day, lest his disciples come and steal him and say to the people, ‘He has been raised from the dead,’ and the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “You have a guard; go, make it as secure as you know how.”

cmp.note: 这半句可以读成「你们有卫兵」（指他们自己的人），也可以读成「给你们一队卫兵」（彼拉多拨给他们的兵）。从 28:14 看，这些卫兵归总督管。白话和英文照字面译成「你们有卫兵」。
cmp.en: The clause can be read as "You have a guard" (their own men) or as "Take a guard" (soldiers Pilate assigns to them). From 28:14 the guards appear to answer to the governor. Both translations keep the literal "You have a guard."

verses.en: And they went and made the tomb secure, sealing the stone, with the guard.

chapters.title: Chapter 28 · The Empty Tomb, the Risen Jesus, the Mountain in Galilee
chapters.intro: At dawn after the Sabbath the two Marys go to see the tomb. In an earthquake an angel rolls back the stone, says Jesus has been raised and sends them to tell the disciples; on the way Jesus himself meets them. The chief priests pay the guards to say that the disciples stole the body. The eleven disciples see Jesus on a mountain in Galilee, and he sends them to make disciples of all the nations.

verses.en: Now after the Sabbath, as it was dawning toward the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And look, there was a great earthquake; for an angel of the Lord, coming down from heaven and approaching, rolled away the stone and was sitting on it.
And his appearance was like lightning, and his clothing white as snow.
And for fear of him those keeping watch shook and became like dead men.
But the angel answered and said to the women, “Do not be afraid, you; for I know that you are looking for Jesus who was crucified.
He is not here, for he has been raised, just as he said. Come, see the place where he was lying.
And go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has been raised from the dead, and look, he is going ahead of you into Galilee; there you will see him.’ Look, I have told you.”
And departing quickly from the tomb with fear and great joy, they ran to tell his disciples.
And look, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” And they came up and took hold of his feet and worshiped him.
Then Jesus says to them, “Do not be afraid; go, tell my brothers to go to Galilee, and there they will see me.”
Now while they were going, look, some of the guard went into the city and reported to the chief priests all that had happened.
And having gathered with the elders and taken counsel, they gave a large sum of silver to the soldiers,
saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came by night and stole him while we were sleeping.’
And if this is heard before the governor, we will persuade him and keep you out of trouble.”
And taking the silver, they did as they were instructed. And this story has been spread among Jews to this very day.
Now the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain to which Jesus had directed them.
And seeing him they worshiped, but some doubted.
And Jesus came up and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
Go therefore and make disciples of all the nations, baptizing them into the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep all that I have commanded you; and look, I am with you all the days, until the end of the age.”

title: The Gospel according to Matthew
summary: The first book of the New Testament: the story of Jesus, whom Christians hold to be the deliverer sent by God, from his family line and birth to his death and resurrection, with long stretches of his teaching, including the Sermon on the Mount. 28 chapters.

primer.a: 基督教圣经的新约开头有四卷「福音书」，各自把耶稣的事讲了一遍，《马太福音》排在第一卷。一般认为它写在公元 80 到 90 年前后，用的是当时通行的希腊文，而且用了更早的《马可福音》作底子：马可讲过的事，这里大部分都有，另外多了耶稣出生的故事和大段的教导。书里没有写作者的名字；传统上说作者是马太，耶稣十二个门徒之一，原来是个税吏。
全书是一个讲故事的人在叙述，他自己不出场。引号里的话是故事里的人说的，其中耶稣的话占了很大的篇幅：有五处他一口气讲了一整章甚至几章（第 5–7 章、第 10 章、第 13 章、第 18 章、第 24–25 章），这些地方每章的导读会提醒「这一章都是耶稣在说」。叙述里的「他」，大多数时候指耶稣。
故事发生在大约公元 30 年前后，地点是地中海东岸的犹太人地区（今天的以色列、巴勒斯坦一带），当时归罗马帝国管。犹太人只拜一位上帝，照着祖先摩西传下来的律法过日子，把古代的律法书、先知书等合称为「经」（就是后来基督徒说的旧约）。很多人在盼望上帝照着经上的应许派一位救主来，这位救主希伯来话叫「弥赛亚」，希腊话叫「基督」，人们认为他会是古代君王大卫的后代。

primer.q: 读的时候会卡住的地方
primer.a: 一是开头就是一长串人名：那是耶稣的家谱，从犹太人的始祖亚伯拉罕一路排到他，用意是说明他是大卫的后代；不想看可以从第 1 章第 18 节读起。二是书里一再说「这是要应验先知的话」，然后引一句旧约：作者是在说，耶稣身上发生的事，经上早就写了。三是「天国」：这卷书多半不说「上帝的国」而说「天国」，是同一个意思，指上帝亲自作王的局面，不是指人死后去的地方。四是耶稣常常打比方，大多数比方书里并不解释是什么意思；读到这样的地方，原文本来就没有说明。五是有些话说得很重（比如第 23 章骂文士和法利赛人），本站照原文译，不加缓和也不加评论。
这些词在书里反复出现，先认一下。
terms: 福音
字面是「好消息」。书里指耶稣带来的消息：天国近了。
基督
希腊话，意思是「受膏的人」，就是上帝选立的那一位救主；希伯来话叫弥赛亚。后来成了耶稣的称号。
天国
字面是「诸天的国」，和别的福音书说的「上帝的国」是一回事：上帝亲自作王、他的心意行得通的局面。
人子
耶稣说到自己时最常用的称呼。字面是「人的儿子」，也是旧约里一位从上帝那里得到权柄的人物的称号。
门徒
跟着耶稣学的人。其中他特别选出十二个。
律法
上帝通过摩西颁给犹太人的规矩，写在旧约开头的五卷书里。「律法和先知」合起来就是指整部旧约。
先知
替上帝传话的人。旧约里有许多卷书记着他们的话，这卷书常常引用。
法利赛人
犹太人里严守律法和各种规矩的一派，在书里常常和耶稣争论。
文士
专门抄写、讲解犹太律法的学者。
义
照上帝的心意去活、去做。书里说的「义人」就是这样的人。

primer.a: 全书 28 章。顺着读的话：第 1–4 章是耶稣的出生和出来传道以前的事；第 5–7 章是最有名的一段教导，通常叫「登山宝训」；第 8–20 章讲他在加利利一带治病、教导，然后走向耶路撒冷；第 21–28 章是他在耶路撒冷的最后一个星期：被捕、钉十字架、复活。只想先读一段的话，读第 5–7 章。

primerEn.q: What kind of book this is
primerEn.a: The New Testament of the Christian Bible opens with four "Gospels," each telling the story of Jesus; Matthew comes first. It is generally dated to around 80 to 90 CE, was written in the common Greek of the time, and is generally thought to have used the earlier Gospel of Mark as its base: most of what Mark tells is here too, along with an account of Jesus’s birth and long stretches of teaching. The book does not name its author; by tradition he was Matthew, one of the twelve disciples, formerly a tax collector.

A narrator tells the whole story and never appears in it. Words in quotation marks are spoken by people in the story, and a large share of them are Jesus’s: in five places he speaks for a whole chapter or several (chapters 5–7, 10, 13, 18, and 24–25). The introduction to each of those chapters says so. "He" in the narration is usually Jesus.

The story takes place around 30 CE in the Jewish lands on the eastern shore of the Mediterranean (today’s Israel and Palestine), then under the Roman Empire. Jews worshiped one God, lived by the law handed down from their ancestor Moses, and called their ancient books of law and prophets "the scriptures" (what Christians later called the Old Testament). Many were waiting for God to send the deliverer those scriptures promised, called "Messiah" in Hebrew and "Christ" in Greek, who was expected to be a descendant of the ancient king David.

First, the book opens with a long list of names: it is Jesus’s family line, from Abraham, the first ancestor of the Jews, down to him, meant to show that he descends from David. You can start at 1:18 if you prefer. Second, the book keeps saying "this was to fulfill what was spoken by the prophet" and then quotes the Old Testament: the author’s point is that what happened to Jesus had already been written. Third, "the kingdom of heaven": this book mostly says that instead of "the kingdom of God"; it means the same thing, the state of affairs in which God himself rules, not a place people go after death. Fourth, Jesus often speaks in comparisons, and the book leaves most of them unexplained; where a saying is puzzling, the original usually gives no explanation either. Fifth, some passages are harsh (chapter 23, against the scribes and Pharisees, for one); this site translates them as they stand, without softening and without comment.
These words recur throughout the book.
terms: Good news (gospel)
In this book, the news Jesus brings: the kingdom of heaven has come near.
Christ
Greek for "anointed one," the deliverer chosen by God; "Messiah" in Hebrew. It later became a title for Jesus.
Kingdom of heaven
Literally "kingdom of the heavens," the same as "kingdom of God" in the other Gospels: the state of affairs in which God himself rules and his will is done.
Son of Man
The name Jesus most often uses for himself. Literally "son of a human being," it is also the title of a figure in the Old Testament who receives authority from God.
Disciples
Those who follow Jesus and learn from him. He singles out twelve of them.
The law
The rules God gave the Jews through Moses, written in the first five books of the Old Testament. "The law and the prophets" together means the whole Old Testament.
Prophets
People who speak for God. Many Old Testament books record their words, and this Gospel quotes them often.
Pharisees
A Jewish group strict about keeping the law and its many rules; in this book they often argue with Jesus.
Scribes
Scholars who copied and explained the Jewish law.
Righteousness
Living and acting as God wants. "The righteous" in this book are people who do.

primerEn.a: The book has 28 chapters. Read straight through: chapters 1–4 cover Jesus’s birth and what came before his public work; chapters 5–7 are his best-known teaching, usually called the Sermon on the Mount; chapters 8–20 follow him healing and teaching around Galilee and then heading for Jerusalem; chapters 21–28 are his last week there: arrest, crucifixion, resurrection. If you want just one stretch, read chapters 5–7.

compare: 希腊文原文用 SBL Greek New Testament（SBLGNT），只去掉了底本里的校勘符号，经文本身没有动；罗马转写是本站按通行规则机械生成的，不标重音。
白话是写给完全没接触过圣经的人看的：用平常说话的词，把谁在对谁说写清楚。原文没有、但不补就看不懂的字，一律放在圆括号（）里；括号里是通行的解释，不是经文本身。英文版贴着字面译，不加括号，两版对着看就知道哪些是补的。白话、英文和所有说明都是 AI 从希腊文译写的，没有经过圣经学者或教会审阅。
对照栏是 1919 年出版的官话和合译本（和合本），录文取自维基文库，繁体转成简体，几个异体字改成了通行写法，原书的旧式标点照录。维基文库录的是称「神」的版本；本站的白话写「上帝」。人名、地名跟和合本走，只有几处用了今天更常见的写法：约旦河、撒旦、凯撒（和合本作「约但河」「撒但」「该撒」）；和合本的「夫子」本站写「老师」，「外邦人」写「外族人」。
和合本当年依据的希腊文底本和 SBLGNT 不完全一样，所以有的地方三栏对不上，不是译错。最显眼的是第 6 章第 13 节：和合本的主祷文末尾多一句「因为国度、权柄、荣耀，全是你的，直到永远」，本站的底本没有。另有三节（17:21、18:11、23:14）底本没有、和合本有（后两节和合本印成小字注），本站留着节号，原文栏放一个「—」。这些地方都在那一节下面的「三语对照」里写明。
这卷书和《马可福音》有大量平行的段落。两卷书希腊文一样的地方，本站尽量用一样的译法；希腊文不一样的地方，译文也跟着不一样，没有互相拉齐。书里引旧约的地方很多，白话照这卷书的希腊文译，所以和旧约原处的字句常有出入，出处写在对照注里。
compareEn: The Greek is the SBL Greek New Testament (SBLGNT) with its text-critical sigla removed and nothing else changed; the romanization is generated mechanically by this site under the usual conventions, without accents.

The Chinese is written for readers who have never opened a Bible: everyday words, with who is speaking to whom made explicit. Words that are not in the Greek but are needed to follow it are put in parentheses; they give the usual explanation and are not part of the text. The English stays close to the wording and adds no parentheses, so reading the two side by side shows what was supplied. The Chinese, the English and all the notes were translated and written by AI from the Greek and have not been reviewed by biblical scholars or by any church.

The older Chinese version shown alongside is the Mandarin Union Version of 1919, taken from Chinese Wikisource, converted to simplified characters with a few variant characters normalized and its original punctuation kept. Wikisource carries the edition that calls God 神 (Shén); this site’s plain Chinese writes 上帝 (Shàngdì). Names follow the Union Version, except for a few now more commonly written another way: the Jordan, Satan and Caesar.

The Union Version was made from a Greek text that differs in places from SBLGNT, so where the columns disagree it is not always a mistranslation. The most visible case is 6:13: the Union Version’s Lord’s Prayer ends with "for yours is the kingdom and the power and the glory forever," which this site’s edition lacks. Three verses (17:21; 18:11; 23:14) are in the Union Version but not in this edition (the last two as small-print notes); the verse numbers are kept, with a dash in the Greek column. Each such place is explained in the note under that verse.

This Gospel has many passages parallel to Mark. Where the Greek of the two is the same, this site tries to translate it the same way; where the Greek differs, the translations differ too and have not been harmonized. The book quotes the Old Testament often; the translation follows this Gospel’s Greek, so the wording often differs from the Old Testament passage itself, whose reference is given in the notes.
